===Washington Redskins===
====2014 season====
The [[2014 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]] selected Breeland in the fourth round (102nd overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=March 18, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was the tenth [[cornerback]] drafted in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Czarda |first=Stephen |date=May 10, 2014 |title=Washington Adds Another Ball-Hawk In Bashaud Breeland |url=http://blog.redskins.com/2014/05/10/washington-adds-another-ball-hawk-in-bashaud-breeland/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160909231629/http://blog.redskins.com/2014/05/10/washington-adds-another-ball-hawk-in-bashaud-breeland/ |archive-date=September 9, 2016 |access-date=May 10, 2014 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref>

On May 16, 2014, the Redskins signed Breeland to a four-year, $2.70 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $486,000.<ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Bashaud Breeland contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/green-bay-packers/bashaud-breeland-14513/ |access-date=November 25, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Mike |date=May 16, 2014 |title=Redskins sign six of eight draft picks to rookie deals |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2014/05/16/redskins-sign-six-of-eight-draft-picks-to-rookie-deals/ |access-date=May 17, 2014 |website=WashingtonPost.com}}</ref> Throughout [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Breeland competed for a roster spot as a backup cornerback against [[Tracy Porter]], [[E. J. Biggers]], [[Chase Minnifield]], and [[Richard Crawford (American football)|Richard Crawford]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jones |first=Mike |date=July 24, 2014 |title=Now healthy, Tracy Porter joins defensive back competition |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/football-insider/wp/2014/07/29/now-healthy-tracy-porter-joins-defensive-back-competition/ |access-date=August 14, 2020 |newspaper=Washington Post}}</ref> Head coach [[Jay Gruden]] named Breeland the fifth cornerback on the depth chart to start the regular season, behind [[DeAngelo Hall]], [[David Amerson]], Biggers, and Porter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dudko |first=James |date=September 1, 2014 |title=Washington Redskins 2014 Virtual Program: Depth-Chart Analysis and More |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2182597-washington-redskins-2014-virtual-program-depth-chart-analysis-and-more |access-date=August 14, 2020 |website=BleacherReport.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut and first career start in the Redskins’ season-opener at the [[Houston Texans]], and made one solo tackle in the 17–6 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Washington Redskins at Houston Texans – September 7th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409070htx.htm |access-date=September 24, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Breeland started the game at strong safety after [[Brandon Meriweather]] was suspended for the first two games of the season. On September 25, 2014, Breeland started at cornerback after Hall sustained a [[Achilles tendon rupture|ruptured Achilles]] the previous game and was subsequently placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jones |first=Mike |date=September 24, 2014 |title=Jim Haslett 'excited' to see Bashaud Breeland in a starting role |work=WashingtonPost.com |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2014/09/24/jim-haslett-excited-to-see-bashaud-breeland-in-a-starting-role/ |access-date=January 2, 2015}}</ref> The former made two solo tackles as the Redskins lost 45–14 against the [[New York Giants]] in Week 4. On October 17, Breeland recorded five solo tackles, a [[pass deflection]], and made his first career interception during a 19–17 victory against the [[Tennessee Titans]]; Breeland intercepted a pass from [[quarterback]] [[Charlie Whitehurst]] originally intended for tight end [[Delanie Walker]] in the second quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2014 |title=Redskins-Titans Monday Stats Pack |url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Titans-Monday-Stats-Pack/f624e8e4-6539-40c7-8426-1b7514145fff |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170817080531/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Titans-Monday-Stats-Pack/f624e8e4-6539-40c7-8426-1b7514145fff |archive-date=August 17, 2017 |access-date=January 2, 2015 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref> He had a breakout performance in a Week 8 win against the [[Dallas Cowboys]]: he covered starting [[wide receiver]] [[Dez Bryant]], limiting him to only three receptions; forced [[DeMarco Murray]] to fumble, which was recovered by safety Meriweather; and broke up a pass on fourth down, sealing the Redskins' overtime victory.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bullock |first=Mark |date=October 30, 2014 |title=Here's how well cornerback Bashaud Breeland played on Monday night |work=WashingtonPost.com |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2014/10/30/heres-how-well-cornerback-bashaud-breeland-played-on-monday-night/ |access-date=January 2, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=El-Bashir |first=Tarik |date=October 28, 2014 |title=Breeland bests Bryant in breakout performance against Cowboys |url=http://www.csnwashington.com/redskinsblog/breeland-bests-bryant-breakout-performance-against-cowboys |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141220075123/http://www.csnwashington.com/redskinsblog/breeland-bests-bryant-breakout-performance-against-cowboys |archive-date=December 20, 2014 |website=CSNWashington.com}}</ref> In their Week 16 game against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], he intercepted quarterback [[Mark Sanchez]] late in the fourth quarter to help seal the Redskins' victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Andrew |date=December 20, 2014 |title=Redskins Drop Eagles 27–24 In FedExField Thriller |url=https://www.washingtonfootball.com/news/redskins-drop-eagles-27-24-in-fedexfield-thriller-14622083 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170817080720/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Drop-Eagles-27-24-In-FedExField-Thriller/63d4439e-a718-408e-8a23-d0f00a9aa9c5 |archive-date=August 17, 2017 |access-date=October 27, 2021 |website=Washington Football Team}}</ref>

On December 31, Washington announced their decision to mutually part ways with defensive coordinator [[Jim Haslett]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2014 |title=Jim Haslett out as Redskins' defensive coordinator |url=https://www.dailyherald.com/article/20141231/sports/312319936/ |access-date=August 16, 2020 |website=DailyHerald.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Breeland completed his rookie season with 66 combined tackles (57 solo), 14 pass deflections, two forced fumbles, and two interceptions in 16 games with 15 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bashaud Breeland 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BreeBa00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=March 18, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2015 season====
Breeland entered training camp slated as a starting cornerback and competed against DeAngelo Hall to retain the role.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barksdale |first=Maurice |date=July 9, 2015 |title=Top 32 Redskins of 2015: Bashaud Breeland |url=https://riggosrag.com/2015/07/09/top-32-redskins-of-2015-bashaud-breeland/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150805052124/http://riggosrag.com/2015/07/09/top-32-redskins-of-2015-bashaud-breeland/ |archive-date=August 5, 2015 |access-date=August 16, 2020 |website=Riggo's Rag|publisher=FanSided}}</ref> On July 31, 2015, the NFL suspended Breeland for the first game of the [[2015 NFL season]] after he was cited by [[Virginia Commonwealth University]] police for possession of [[marijuana]] on August 11, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keim |first=John |date=August 13, 2014 |title=Bashaud Breeland cited for marijuana |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/11350137/bashaud-breeland-washington-redskins-cited-marijuana-possession|access-date=October 27, 2021 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Keim |first=John |date=July 31, 2015 |title=Bashaud Breeland suspended 1 game; CB out 4–6 weeks for MCL, source says |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13353220/bashaud-breeland-washington-redskins-suspended-opener |access-date=October 27, 2021 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On the same day, Breeland was injured during the second day of training camp during practice and was carted off the field. It was later announced that he sprained his [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] and was expected to recover in four-to-six weeks; he was not able to participate for the rest of training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=July 31, 2015 |title=Redskins CB Bashaud Breeland injures MCL |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/redskins-cb-bashaud-breeland-injures-mcl-0ap3000000505357 |access-date=July 31, 2015 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

In Week 5, he recorded his first interception of the [[2015 Washington Redskins season|season]] against [[Atlanta Falcons]]' quarterback [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 12, 2015 |title=Redskins-Falcons Monday Stats Pack |url=https://www.washingtonfootball.com/news/redskins-falcons-monday-stats-pack-16058690 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171028094120/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Falcons-Monday-Stats-Pack/3e5ce0ca-3591-42a0-a954-8b2cbae579ed |archive-date=October 28, 2017 |access-date=October 27, 2021 |website=Washington Football Team}}</ref> In Week 6, Breeland had a solid performance against the [[New York Jets]], having recorded one interception, one forced fumble, and two fumble recoveries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Andrew |date=October 18, 2015 |title=Redskins Fall To Jets, 34–20 |access-date=October 27, 2021 |website=Washington Football Team}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 19, 2015 |title=Redskins-Jets Monday Stats Pack Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2016 season====
[[File:Jarius Wright 2016 vs. Redskins.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Breeland (right) playing against the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in 2016]]
Despite having a difficult time covering wide receiver [[Antonio Brown]] in their Week 1 loss to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], Breeland recorded his first interception of the season against quarterback [[Ben Roethlisberger]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Czarda |first=Stephen |date=September 13, 2016 |title=Bashaud Breeland Will Learn And Grow From Steelers Game |url=https://www.washingtonfootball.com/news/bashaud-breeland-will-learn-and-grow-from-steelers-game-17678418|access-date=October 27, 2021 |website=Washington Football Team}}</ref> In a Week 16 win against the [[Chicago Bears]], he recorded two interceptions on quarterback [[Matt Barkley]], which made him the first Redskins player since [[Fred Smoot]] (2001) to start his career recording multiple interceptions in three consecutive seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kring-Schreifels |first=Jake |date=December 24, 2016 |title=Redskins Defense Produces Five Interceptions In Victory Over Bears |url=https://www.washingtonfootball.com/news/redskins-defense-produces-five-interceptions-in-victory-over-bears-18334295 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805100954/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Defense-Produces-Five-Interceptions-In-Victory-Over-Bears/33ae532d-254a-4c73-ba10-2f6f9556d87d |archive-date=August 5, 2017 |access-date=October 27, 2021 |website=Washington Football Team}}</ref> He finished the 2016 season with 73 total tackles, three interceptions, 11 passes defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bashaud Breeland 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BreeBa00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2017 season====
Breeland recorded the first interception of the [[2017 Washington Redskins season|2017 season]] against backup quarterback [[Kellen Clemens]] in their Week 14 loss to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]]; he ran the ball 96 yards for a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kring-Schreifels |first=Jake |date=December 10, 2017 |title=For Breeland And Davis, Milestone Plays Muted By Loss To Chargers |url=https://www.washingtonfootball.com/news/for-breeland-and-davis-milestone-plays-muted-by-loss-to-chargers-19955489 |access-date=October 27, 2021 |website=Washington Football Team}}</ref>

Following the season, Breeland became an [[unrestricted free agent]]. On March 16, 2018, Breeland agreed to terms with the [[Carolina Panthers]] on a three-year, $24 million contract, including $11 million in guaranteed money.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=March 13, 2018 |title=Carolina Panthers expected to sign Bashaud Breeland |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000921005/article/carolina-panthers-expected-to-sign-bashaud-breeland |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200314162139/https://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000921005/article/carolina-panthers-expected-to-sign-bashaud-breeland |archive-date=March 14, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> However, he failed his physical after suffering an infected cut on his foot in the [[Dominican Republic]]; the contract was therefore voided and he became a free agent again.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=March 16, 2018 |title=Bashaud Breeland fails physical; Panthers deal void |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bashaud-breeland-fails-physical-panthers-deal-void-0ap3000000921767 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190912132042/https://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000921767/article/bashaud-breeland-fails-physical-wont-sign-with-panthers |archive-date=September 12, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
====2018 season====
On September 25, 2018, the [[Green Bay Packers]] signed Breeland to a one-year, $880,000 contract that includes a signing bonus of $90,000.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Demovsky |first=Rob |date=September 25, 2018 |title=Davon House to have season-ending shoulder surgery; Packers bring on Bashaud Breeland |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/24796581/packers-db-davon-house-shoulder-surgery |access-date=September 26, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Breeland was signed after cornerback [[Davon House]] sustained a shoulder injury and was placed on [[Injured reserve list|injured reserve]]. Head coach [[Mike McCarthy]] named Breeland the fifth cornerback on the depth chart, behind [[Tramon Williams]], [[Kevin King (American football)|Kevin King]], [[Josh Jackson (cornerback)|Josh Jackson]], and [[Jaire Alexander]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Green Bay Packers (2018) |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/213/GB |access-date=August 16, 2020 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

Breeland's first game as a Packer was a 17–31 loss to the [[New England Patriots]] in Week 9, after missing several weeks of play to learn the playbook.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots – November 4th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201811040nwe.htm |access-date=September 23, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 10 against the [[Miami Dolphins]], Breeland recorded his first interception of the season off backup quarterback [[Brock Osweiler]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Dolphins at Green Bay Packers – November 11th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201811110gnb.htm |access-date=September 23, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He injured his groin in Week 11 against the [[Seattle Seahawks]] and missed the next two games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Demovsky |first=Rob |date=November 15, 2018 |title=Biggest injury questions for all 32 teams in Week 11 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/25278069/nfl-biggest-injury-questions-all-32-teams-week-11-2018 |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Breeland returned in the Week 14 game against the Atlanta Falcons, where he recorded a 22-yard [[Interception#Gridiron football|pick-six]] off Falcons' quarterback Matt Ryan, while also having a fumble recovery in the same game that helped seal a 34–20 win for the Packers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Green Bay Packers – December 9th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812090gnb.htm |access-date=September 23, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
====2019 season====
On March 18, 2019, the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] signed Breeland to a one-year, $2 million contract that includes a signing bonus of $1.15 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maya |first=Adam |date=March 18, 2019 |title=Chiefs signing CB Bashaud Breeland to one-year deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chiefs-sign-cb-bashaud-breeland-to-one-year-deal-0ap3000001023156 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200127065934/https://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001023156/article/chiefs-signing-cb-bashaud-breeland-to-oneyear-deal |archive-date=January 27, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Andy Reid]] named Breeland a starting cornerback to begin the regular season, alongside former Redskins' teammate [[Kendall Fuller]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Kansas City Chiefs: 09/02/2019 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/224/KC |access-date=August 17, 2020 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

In Week 2 against the [[Oakland Raiders]], Breeland intercepted [[Derek Carr]] in the end zone as the Chiefs won 28–10.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 15, 2019 |title=Mahomes' 4 TDs in 2nd quarter lead Chiefs past Raiders 28–10 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128118 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In Week 4 against the [[Detroit Lions]], Breeland recovered a fumble by running back [[Kerryon Johnson]] in the end zone and returned it 100 yards for a touchdown in the 34–30 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 29, 2019 |title=Chiefs score late, stay undefeated with 34–30 win over Lions |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128023 |access-date=September 29, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Additionally, in Week 14, Breeland made a game-winning pass deflection against the Patriots on fourth down; the win allowed the Chiefs to clinch the [[AFC West]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fedotin |first=Jeff |date=December 8, 2019 |title=Bashaud Breeland Saves The Day In Chiefs' Epic Win Over Patriots |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jefffedotin/2019/12/08/baushad-breeland-saves-the-day-in-the-chiefs-epic-win/ |access-date=September 23, 2020 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 9, 2019 |title=KC survives errors, takes AFC West with 23-16 win over Pats |url=https://apnews.com/article/0c4aa256515cb4e64bde93327339f856 |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> He finished the 2019 season with 48 total tackles, two interceptions, eight passes defended, and two fumble recoveries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bashaud Breeland 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BreeBa00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In [[Super Bowl LIV]] against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], Breeland recorded a team-high seven tackles and intercepted a pass by quarterback [[Jimmy Garoppolo]] during the 31–20 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2020 |title=Mahomes leads Chiefs' rally past 49ers in Super Bowl, 31–20 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401131047 |access-date=February 2, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

====2020 season====
On April 14, 2020, the Chiefs signed Breeland to a one-year, $3 million contract that includes a signing bonus of $1.50 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Reggie |date=April 14, 2020 |title=Returning for another run – former Clemson defensive back is back with the Chiefs |url=https://www.wltx.com/article/sports/nfl/101-ed45e811-e334-4c9e-ba23-82c30bc78e67 |access-date=April 14, 2020 |website=wltx.com}}</ref> He was suspended the first four games of the 2020 season for violating the league's policy on substance abuse, and was placed on the reserve/suspended list on September 5.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Chiefs Roster Down to NFL-Mandated 53 |url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/chiefs-roster-down-to-nfl-mandated-53-x6671 |access-date=September 12, 2020 |website=Chiefs.com}}</ref> He was reinstated from suspension on October 6,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldman |first=Charles |date=October 6, 2020 |title=Chiefs CB Bashaud Breeland returns from four-game suspension this week |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2020/10/06/kansas-city-chiefs-bashaud-breeland-four-game-suspension-lifted-this-week/ |access-date=March 18, 2021 |website=Chiefs Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> and activated to the roster on October 10.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=October 10, 2020 |title=Chiefs activate Bashaud Breeland from suspended list |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/10/10/chiefs-activate-bashaud-breeland-from-suspended-list/ |access-date=October 26, 2020 |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2020 season with 38 total tackles, two interceptions, nine passes defended, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bashaud Breeland 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BreeBa00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=March 18, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
Breeland signed with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on June 8, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Eric |date=June 4, 2021 |title=Vikings Agree to Terms with CB Bashaud Breeland |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/bashaud-breeland-roster-agree-terms |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 NFL Transactions: Signings – June |url=https://www.nfl.com/transactions/league/signings/2021/6 |access-date=June 16, 2021 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He entered the 2021 season as a starting cornerback alongside [[Patrick Peterson]]. In Week 14, Breeland had eight tackles and intercepted quarterback Ben Roethlisberger in a 36–28 win over the Steelers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Minnesota Vikings - December 9th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202112090min.htm |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On December 18, Breeland was waived by the Vikings after getting into a verbal altercation with coaches and teammates at practice earlier that day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tomasson |first=Chris |date=December 18, 2021 |title=Vikings waive cornerback Bashaud Breeland after altercation at practice |url=https://www.twincities.com/2021/12/18/vikings-waive-cornerback-bashaud-breeland-after-altercation-at-practice/ |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Cronin |first=Courtney |author-link=Courtney Cronin |date=December 18, 2021 |title=CB Bashaud Breeland waived by Minnesota Vikings after verbal altercation at practice, source says |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32896907/minnesota-vikings-waive-starting-cb-bashaud-breeland |accessdate=December 21, 2021 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> He finished the 2021 season with 63 total tackles, two interceptions, five passes defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bashaud Breeland 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BreeBa00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On January 4, 2022, Breeland was signed to the [[Arizona Cardinals]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=January 4, 2022 |title=Cardinals Sign Veteran Bashaud Breeland To Practice Squad |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-bashaud-breeland-dj-humphries-markus-golden-activated |access-date=July 10, 2023 |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref>  His contract expired when the team's season ended on January 17.

==Personal life==
Breeland was arrested on April 28, 2020, for multiple charges, including resisting arrest, having alcohol in a motor vehicle with the seal broken, having an open container of beer or wine in a motor vehicle, possession of 28 grams or less of marijuana or 10 grams of hash, and driving without a license. The police officer who detained Breeland alleged that Breeland threw a “large blunt” into his car and he pushed the deputy out of the way and attempted to flee the officer before he was detained. Police found marijuana in the car as well as open bottles of beer and tequila. The morning after the arrest, he posted to his Twitter that the marijuana was thrown into his car, but quickly deleted the tweets. The arresting officer said that Breeland informed him that he was a “marijuana enthusiast”. Breeland was already facing a suspension for a failed drug test prior to the arrest.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teicher |first=Adam |date=April 28, 2020 |title=Chiefs CB Bashaud Breeland arrested, also facing NFL suspension |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/29110216/chiefs-cornerback-bashaud-breeland-jail-south-carolina-arrest |access-date=September 23, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He pleaded guilty on October 2, 2020, and received a 30-day suspended jail sentence and $100 fine for each charge.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Palmer |first=Tod |date=October 2, 2020 |title=Chiefs CB Bashaud Breeland pleads guilty to disorderly conduct, possession in South Carolina |url=https://www.kshb.com/sports/chiefs-cb-bashaud-breeland-pleads-guilty-to-disorderly-conduct-possession-in-south-carolina |access-date=March 18, 2021 |website=KSHB.com}}</ref>

Breeland was arrested again on August 7, 2023, in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]] after police pulled him over and discovered the 2020 Mercedes Benz G550 SUV he was driving had been reported stolen in Florida. Officers searched the car and located a swath of concealed firearms, including multiple assault rifles and several handguns. According to the charging document, police also found copious amounts of drugs in the vehicle.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hills |first=Connor |date=August 9, 2023 |title=Former starting corner and Chiefs Super Bowl champ facing numerous criminal charges |url=https://www.kmbc.com/article/bashaud-breeland-corner-chiefs-arrested-charged/44775765# |access-date=August 9, 2023 |website=KMBC.com.com}}</ref>

Breeland was arrested again on April 7, 2024, in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]] after a call concerning drug activity. Police found Breeland with a variety of drugs at the scene.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jennes |first1=Logan |title=Ex-Super Bowl champ found with firearms and drugs assaults Charlotte officers during arrest: reports |url=https://www.qcnews.com/charlotte/ex-super-bowl-champ-found-with-firearms-and-drugs-assaults-charlotte-officers-during-arrest-reports/ |access-date=30 April 2024 |work=Queen City News |date=30 April 2024}}</ref>

'''Beau Christian Allen''' (born November 14, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin Badgers]] and was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the seventh round of the [[2014 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Beau attended [[Minnetonka High School]], graduating in 2010. He was the only Minnetonka student in history to start all four years under coach Dave Nelson. He was ranked 5th in the state by the website Rivals. He was recruited by Notre Dame, Stanford, Michigan, UCLA, amongst others. He ultimately chose Wisconsin as that is the alma mater of his parents.

==College career==
In his last three years at [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin]], Allen had eight sacks and 15 tackles for loss.<ref name=fouryear/><ref name=Wisconsin>{{cite web|title=Beau Allen|url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/beau_allen_712837.html|work=[[Wisconsin Badgers]]|publisher=[[University of Wisconsin]]|access-date=May 12, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140417114934/http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/beau_allen_712837.html|archive-date=April 17, 2014}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
[[File:Joe Thuney and Beau Allen Super Bowl LII 85F9D5D.jpg|thumb|right|Allen (number 94) in [[Super Bowl LII]]]]
Allen was selected in the seventh round (224th overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]] by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On May 15, 2014, he signed a four-year deal with the Eagles.<ref name=fouryear>{{cite news |title=Eagles sign Beau Allen to four-year deal |url=http://www.csnphilly.com/football-philadelphia-eagles/eagles-sign-beau-allen-four-year-deal |access-date=May 15, 2014 |newspaper=CSNPhilly.com |date=May 15, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517055416/http://www.csnphilly.com/football-philadelphia-eagles/eagles-sign-beau-allen-four-year-deal |archive-date=May 17, 2014 }}</ref> As a rookie in 2014, Allen played all 16 games with 10 tackles and half a sack. In 2015, he played 16 games with 2 starts, finishing the year with 28 tackles and 2 passes defended.{{citation needed|date=October 2018}}

On September 11, 2016, in a game against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Allen played situational snaps at [[fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]], while still rotating in for plays on defense. The Eagles were able to score a rushing touchdown behind Allen's blocking, while he also had a tackle on defense.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kulp |first=Andrew |date=September 12, 2016 |title=Beau Allen has ‘a blast' subbing in as Eagles fullback |url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nfl/beau-allen-has-a-blast-subbing-in-as-eagles-fullback/354314/ |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=NBC Sports Philadelphia |language=en}}</ref> Beau finished the 2016 year with 29 tackles and 0.5 sacks.{{citation needed|date=October 2018}}

On April 8, 2017, it was reported that Allen had suffered a pectoral injury that required 4–6 weeks to recover.<ref name="h100">{{cite web | title=Eagles DT Beau Allen suffers pectoral injury | website=NFL.com | date=2017-04-08 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/eagles-dt-beau-allen-suffers-pectoral-injury-0ap3000000798636 | access-date=2024-10-15}}</ref> Allen had 20 tackles and 1 sack for his 2017 season. Allen recorded 2 tackles in [[Super Bowl LII]] and beat the [[New England Patriots]] 41-33.<ref name="g522">{{cite web | last=Wesseling | first=Chris | title=Philadelphia Eagles knock off Patriots, win Super Bowl | website=NFL.com | date=2018-02-04 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/philadelphia-eagles-knock-off-patriots-win-super-bowl-0ap3000000914459 | access-date=2024-10-15}}</ref>

Allen is also known for carrying his passed out teammate [[Jason Kelce]] out of a Buffalo Billiards bar in Philadelphia after a night of heavy drinking following an Eagles holiday party. Allen has stated that carrying the famed Eagles center on the cobblestone streets "fireman style" was the hardest thing he's ever done because Kelce fought him the entire way.<ref name="essentiallysports">{{cite news |last1=Tiwari |first1=Utkarsh |title=One of the Hardest Things I’ve Ever Done” – Beau Allen Recounts Lifting a “Passed Out” Jason Kelce Out of the Bar on the Center’s First Date With Wife Kylie |url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/nfl-active-news-one-of-the-hardest-things-ive-ever-done-beau-allen-recounts-lifting-a-passed-out-jason-kelce-out-of-the-bar-on-the-centers-first-date-with-wife-kylie/ |access-date=12 October 2024 |work=Essentially Sports |publisher=Full Spectrum Services LLP |date=21 February 2024 |ref=essentiallysports}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On March 15, 2018, Allen signed a three-year contract worth an estimated<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Sign Beau Allen to Strengthen Middle|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Sign-Beau-Allen-to-Strengthen-Middle/72405e86-3476-46f0-ad2e-74950cb5c199|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=March 15, 2018|access-date=March 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315192711/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Bucs-Sign-Beau-Allen-to-Strengthen-Middle/72405e86-3476-46f0-ad2e-74950cb5c199|archive-date=March 15, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> $15 million<ref name="overthecap">{{cite web|title=Beau Allen|url=https://overthecap.com/player/beau-allen/3163|website=Over The Cap|publisher=Over The Cap|access-date=April 8, 2018|ref=overthecap}}</ref> with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. In 13 games, he had 10 tackles and 0.5 sacks.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Leger |first1=Justin |title=Why new DT Beau Allen could soon become a Patriots fan favorite |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/patriots/why-new-dt-beau-allen-could-soon-become-patriots-fan-favorite |access-date=March 19, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 18, 2020}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On March 20, 2020, Allen signed a two-year deal worth up to $8 million with the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Alper |first1=Josh |title=Patriots reach deal with Beau Allen |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/18/patriots-reach-deal-with-beau-allen/ |access-date=March 19, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 18, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 7.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots sign two players to the 53-man roster from the practice squad; place two players on injured reserve|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-two-players-to-the-53-man-roster-from-the-practice-squad-place-two|website=Patriots.com|date=September 7, 2020}}</ref> Allen was designated to return from injured reserve on October 21, and began practicing with the team again;<ref>{{cite news |author=McKenna, Henry |title=Beau Allen, David Andrews and Josh Uche practice for Patriots in Week 7 |url=https://patriotswire.usatoday.com/2020/10/21/patriots-beau-allen-david-andrews-josh-uche-week-7/ |website=USAToday.com |date=October 21, 2020 |access-date=December 17, 2020}}</ref> however, after he suffered an injury in practice, the Patriots declined to activate him after his 21-day practice period expired, and he was ruled out for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Beau Allen Won't Play This Season For Patriots, Bill Belichick Reveals |url=https://boston.cbslocal.com/2020/11/02/beau-allen-will-not-play-for-patriots-this-season/ |website=CBSLocal.com |date=November 2, 2020 |access-date=December 17, 2020}}</ref> Allen was released after the season on March 18, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Michael |title=Patriots cut Marqise Lee, Beau Allen |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/03/18/patriots-cut-marqise-lee-beau-allen/ |publisher=NBC Sports |date=18 March 2021 |access-date=18 March 2021}}</ref>

Allen announced his retirement from professional football on July 1, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/eagles/former-eagles-nt-beau-allen-announces-his-retirement-nfl|website=[[NBC Sports]]|title=Another Super Bowl Eagle announces his retirement|date=July 1, 2022|author=Zangaro, Dave}}</ref>

'''Benjamin James Bronson''' (born September 9, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Arena Football League]] (AFL). He played in the NFL for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] and the AFL for the [[Houston ThunderBears]] and [[Carolina Cobras]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor Bears]].

Bronson also played [[college baseball]] at [[Baylor Bears baseball|Baylor]] and professionally in the [[Kansas City Royals]] organization from 1996 to 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.baseball-reference.com/register/player.fcgi?id=bronso001ben|title=Ben Bronson Minor Leagues Statistics & History|website=Baseball-Reference.com}}</ref>

In 2000, he was named the AFL Breakout Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |title=L.A. Avengers sign AFL veteran Ben Bronson |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/l-a-avengers-sign-afl-veteran-ben-bronson/n-3115827 |website=Our Sports Central |accessdate=September 21, 2018 |date=January 10, 2005}}</ref> Outside of arena football, Bronson appeared in ''[[The Longest Yard (2005 film)|The Longest Yard]]'' (2005).<ref>{{cite web |title=AFL players hit Hollywood in "The Longest Yard". He is also the twin brother of former Track and Field Hurdler Olympian John Byran Bronson.

|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/afl-players-hit-hollywood-in-the-longest-yard/n-3166271 |website=Our Sports Central |accessdate=September 21, 2018 |date=May 23, 2005}}</ref>

Bronson is the twin brother to the former American Olympic 400-meter hurdler, John Bryan Bronson, who won the bronze medal at the 1997 World Championships in Athens. ''[[Bryan Bronson]]''

'''Ben Bredeson''' (born February 20, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was an All-American playing [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]], and drafted by the Ravens in the [[2020 NFL draft]]. Bredeson attended [[Arrowhead High School]], winning Wisconsin [[Gatorade Player of the Year]] and receiving All-American honors by MaxPreps and [[USA Today All-USA high school football team|USA Today]].

==Early life==

He is the son of former [[Illinois State University|Illinois State]] center, Mike Bredeson, and the middle brother of older brother, Jack, and younger brother, [[Max Bredeson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wolverineswire.usatoday.com/2022/09/13/michigan-football-max-bredeson-ben-bredeson/|title=Max Bredeson on his journey to Michigan football|website=WolverinesWire|first=Isaiah|last=Hole|date=September 13, 2022|access-date=February 16, 2024}}</ref> Ben Bredeson played high school football at [[Arrowhead High School]] and made the varsity team in his freshman year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.jsonline.com/sports/preps/arrowheads-ben-bredeson-a-man-among-boys-b99559344z1-322243721.html|title=Arrowhead's Ben Bredeson 'a man among boys'|website=www.jsonline.com}}</ref> As a junior he was a first-team All-State selection. As a senior he was again named to the All-State first-team and received first-team All-American honors by MaxPreps and [[USA Today All-USA high school football team|USA Today]]. Also receiving the Joe Thomas Award, as the top offensive lineman in the state of Wisconsin, and the Gatorade Player of the Year in Wisconsin.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/ben_bredeson_1001399.html |title=Ben Bredeson Bio |website=www.mgoblue.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160207045830/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/ben_bredeson_1001399.html |archive-date=February 7, 2016}}</ref> Bredeson was among the nation's top high school seniors,  invited to the 2016 [[Under Armour All-America Game]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/ben-bredeson-under-armour-all-american-selection-tour|title=Wisconsin giant Ben Bredeson eager to play in Under Armour All-America Game|date=September 10, 2015}}</ref>

After receiving 17 scholarship offers, Bredeson cut down his choices to [[University of Alabama|Alabama]], [[University of Michigan|Michigan]], [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]], [[Ohio State University|Ohio State]], [[Stanford University|Stanford]] and [[University of Wisconsin|Wisconsin]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-football-recruiting/2015/5/5/8556171/ben-bredeson-wisconsin-badgers-michigan-ohio-state-stanford-alabama-notre-dame|title=Can Badgers keep top-30 OT Bredeson close to home?|first=Wescott|last=Eberts|date=May 5, 2015|website=SBNation.com}}</ref> On June 17, 2015, he committed to play for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]].

=== Baltimore Ravens ===
Bredeson was drafted by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the fourth round (143rd overall) of the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Fourth Round (No. 143): Ravens Draft Offensive Lineman Ben Bredeson|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/fourth-round-no-143-ravens-draft-offensive-lineman-ben-bredeson|author=Brown, Clifton|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=April 25, 2020}}</ref>

In his rookie season with the Ravens, Bredeson played in 10 games mostly in a reserve and special teams role and was a [[healthy scratch]] for weeks 1-3, 6-7, and 10.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ben Bredeson 2020 Game Log|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BredBe00.htm|access-date=September 1, 2021|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref>

On January 9, 2021, Bredeson was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite news |author=Mink, Ryan |title=Ravens Activate Sam Koch, Place Ben Bredeson on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-activate-sam-koch-place-ben-bredeson-on-injured-reserve |website=BaltimoreRavens.com |date=January 9, 2021 |access-date=February 16, 2021}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On August 31, 2021, Bredeson was traded to the New York Giants along with a 2022 fifth round pick and a 2023 seventh round pick in exchange for a 2022 fourth round pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Trade Ben Bredeson to New York Giants|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/reports-ravens-trade-ben-bredeson-to-new-york-giants|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=August 31, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Duggan|first=Jeff Zrebiec and Dan|title=Ravens trade OL Ben Bredeson to Giants: Source|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4201244/2021/08/31/ravens-trade-ol-ben-bredeson-to-giants-source/|access-date=October 3, 2021|website=The Athletic|language=en}}</ref> He made his debut for the Giants in week 2 against the [[Washington Football Team]] after [[Nick Gates]] injured his leg.<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 19, 2021|title=How will the New York Giants supplement the massive loss of Nick Gates on offensive line?|url=https://empiresportsmedia.com/new-york-giants/how-will-the-new-york-giants-supplement-the-massive-loss-of-nick-gates-on-offensive-line/|access-date=October 3, 2021|website=Empire Sports Media|language=en-US}}</ref> In Week 3 he made his first career start against the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. During the game he injured his hand and was named inactive the following week against the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 29, 2021|title=Report: Giants' Ben Bredeson could miss time with hand injury|url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2021/09/29/new-york-giants-ben-bredeson-could-miss-time-hand-injury/|access-date=October 3, 2021|website=Giants Wire|language=en-US}}</ref>

Bredeson was named the starting left guard Week 1 of the 2022 season after [[Shane Lemieux]] got injured during the first preseason game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants' Jon Feliciano might know opening-day opponent Titans as well as his own offensive line teammates |url=https://www.nj.com/giants/2022/09/giants-center-jon-feliciano-might-know-opening-day-opponent-tennessee-as-well-as-his-own-offensive-line-teammates.html|author=Brookover, Bob|website=nj.com|date=September 7, 2022}}</ref> On October 29, 2022, he was placed on injured reserve with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Elerson Smith activated, Ben Bredeson to IR among roster moves|url=https://www.giants.com/news/elerson-smith-ben-bredeson-injured-reserve-landon-collins-lawrence-cager-week-8|author=Citak, Matt|website=Giants.com|date=October 29, 2022}}</ref> He was activated on December 17.

Bredeson was named the starting left guard Week 1 of the 2023 season after beating [[Joshua Ezeudu]] during training camp.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mark Glowinski, Ben Bredeson likely to be Giants' starting guards vs. Cowboys|url=https://nypost.com/2023/09/08/daboll-confirms-giants-settled-on-two-starting-guards/|author=Schwartz, Jared|website=nypost.com|date=September 8, 2023}}</ref> On October 15, 2023, Bredeson was moved to right guard after the Giants signed [[Justin Pugh]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Justin Pugh goes from 'couch' to Giants' active roster in 2 weeks|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/38688495/justin-pugh-goes-couch-giants-active-roster-2-weeks|author=Raanan, Jordan|website=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2023}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On March 15, 2024, Bredeson signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Land Former Giants OL Ben Bredeson|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-land-former-giants-ol-ben-bredeson|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=March 15, 2024}}</ref> He was named the Buccaneers starting left guard, starting all 17 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Bredeson 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BredBe00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On March 12, 2025, Bredeson signed a three-year, $22 million contract extension with the Buccaneers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ben Bredeson Adds Continuity in the Trenches|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/ben-bredeson-adds-continuity-in-trenches|author=Dix, Brianna|website=Buccaneers.com|date=March 12, 2025}}</ref> He made 11 starts for the team before suffering a knee injury in Week 14 against the [[2025 New Orleans Saints|New Orleans Saints]]. On December 9, Bredeson was placed on season-ending injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bucs Put Ben Bredeson on IR, Sign Jason Pierre-Paul to Practice Squad|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/jason-pierre-paul-ps-ben-bredeson-ir-roster-move|access-date=January 21, 2026|website=buccaneers.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Ben Braunecker''' (born February 7, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Harvard Crimson football|Harvard Crimson]]. He was signed by the [[Chicago Bears]] as an undrafted free agent in 2016, and played for the team through 2019.

==Early life==
Braunecker attended [[Forest Park High School (Indiana)|Forest Park High School]] in [[Indiana]], where he played for the football team on offense, defense and [[special teams]]. He started for three years and was [[team captain]] for his senior year. In his high school career, Braunecker recorded 51 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 1,254 yards and 16 [[touchdowns]]. As a [[return specialist]], he had 29 [[kickoff returns]] for 1,005 yards, while on defense, he recorded 101 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] and seven [[interceptions]].  He was twice named All-State (Honorable Mention); he was the Southwestern Indiana MVP and twice All-Conference.<ref name="Harvard bio">{{Cite web |title=48 Ben Braunecker |url=http://www.gocrimson.com/sports/fball/2015-16/bios/braunecker_ben_31xk?view=bio |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150719123357/http://gocrimson.com/sports/fball/2015-16/bios/braunecker_ben_31xk?view=bio |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 19, 2015 |access-date=October 1, 2016 |website=[[Harvard Crimson]] }}</ref>

He was also a [[Indiana High School Athletic Association|IHSAA]] State Finalist in the [[discus]] and [[shot put]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Magley | first=Hendrix | title=Bears' Ben Braunecker has a love for football and molecular biology | website=Courier & Press | date=2019-12-01 | url=https://www.courierpress.com/story/sports/2019/12/01/bears-ben-braunecker-has-love-football-and-molecular-biology/3909556002/ | access-date=2025-09-05}}</ref>

==College career==
In his senior year, Braunecker was named a consensus [[All-American]] as he was selected to the [[Associated Press]] [[Football Championship Subdivision]] (FCS) All-America first-team, the [[Walter Camp Football Foundation|Walter Camp]] FCS All-America team, the STATS FCS All-America first-team, [[American Football Coaches Association]] FCS Coaches' All-America team and the College Sporting News Fabulous Fifty FCS All-America team.  He was also honored on the College Sports Madness All-America first-team and the InstantScouting FCS All-America team.
He was also named first-team All-[[Ivy League]] when he recorded 48 catches for 850 yards and eight touchdowns.  He finished his college career with 68 receptions for 1,168 yards and 10 touchdowns.  Harvard won 3 Ivy League titles during his career, compiling a 24–4 conference record and an overall record of 36–4.<ref name="Best">{{Cite news |last=Clegg |first=Jonathan |date=March 1, 2016 |title=The Best Player at the NFL Combine Went to ... Harvard? |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/the-best-player-at-the-nfl-combine-went-to-harvard-1456877247 |access-date=October 1, 2016}}</ref>

Braunecker majored in [[molecular biology|molecular]] and [[cell biology]].<ref name="First career touchdown">{{Cite web |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |date=November 10, 2019 |title=Ben Braunecker's first career touchdown gives Bears much-needed spark |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bears/ben-brauneckers-first-career-touchdown-gives-bears-much-needed-spark |access-date=November 11, 2019 |publisher=[[NBC Sports Chicago]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Braunecker attended the [[NFL Combine]] and was the fastest in the 60-yard shuttle, was ranked second in the [[vertical leap]], [[broad jump]], [[three-cone drill]] and 20-yard shuttle and had the third-highest repetitions in the [[bench press]] of all [[tight ends]].<ref name="Best" /> He was projected by many analysts to be a fourth to sixth round draft selection. NFLDraftScout.com ranked him the sixth best tight end out of the 102 available. He attended Harvard's [[Pro Day]] and was able to beat his combine time and numbers. Braunecker chose to stand on his combine numbers for his 3-cone drill, short shuttle, and bench press.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Braunecker, DS #6 TE, Harvard: 2016 NFL Draft |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=1005889&draftyear=2016&genpos=TE |access-date=December 22, 2016 |website=nfldraftscout.com}}</ref>

Braunecker struggled with a severe ankle injury during the 2016 offseason and missed the entire preseason.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Campbell |first=Rich |date=October 1, 2016 |title=Bears elevate tight end Ben Braunecker to active roster |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/football/bears/ct-bears-ben-braunecker-active-roster-20161001-story.html |access-date=October 1, 2016}}</ref> He was released on September 3,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer, Larry |date=September 3, 2016 |title=Bears trim 22 to reach 53-man limit |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-rostermoves/Bears-trim-22-to-reach-53-man-limit/2eb298bf-b806-403c-8c82-930683de72d9 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171021021223/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-rostermoves/Bears-trim-22-to-reach-53-man-limit/2eb298bf-b806-403c-8c82-930683de72d9 |archive-date=October 21, 2017 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref> but was signed to the [[practice squad]] the following day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=September 4, 2016 |title=Bears sign Paulsen, claim 2 off waivers |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-rostermoves/Bears-sign-Paulsen-claim-2-off-waivers/bf99c94f-4415-41e2-8a7b-1271817f13db |access-date=October 1, 2016 |publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]}}</ref> Going into the regular season, he was the Bears' third option at tight end, behind [[Zach Miller (tight end, born 1984)|Zach Miller]] and [[Logan Paulsen]]. On October 1, 2016, he was promoted to the active roster and was officially named the Bears' third tight end on their depth chart behind veterans Miller and Paulsen.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=October 1, 2016 |title=Braunecker elevated to active roster |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/braunecker-elevated-to-active-roster-17798427 |publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]}}</ref> He made his first NFL start against the [[Green Bay Packers]] on October 20.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Braunecker Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrauBe00.htm |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On September 3, 2017, Braunecker was waived by the Bears and was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer, Larry |date=September 3, 2017 |title=Bears claim three players off waivers |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-claim-three-players-off-waivers/638b3665-97de-4e6c-94cd-980ad3dff5a0 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904201947/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-claim-three-players-off-waivers/638b3665-97de-4e6c-94cd-980ad3dff5a0 |archive-date=September 4, 2017 |access-date=September 4, 2017 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer, Larry |date=September 4, 2017 |title=Bears sign Jenkins, nine to practice squad |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-sign-Jenkins-nine-to-practice-squad/6839c7c6-56dc-4237-9c92-33d3626dedd9 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108100212/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-sign-Jenkins-nine-to-practice-squad/6839c7c6-56dc-4237-9c92-33d3626dedd9 |archive-date=November 8, 2017 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 7, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper, Josh |date=November 7, 2017 |title=Bears promote Ben Braunecker, put Zach Miller on injured reserve |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/11/07/bears-promote-ben-braunecker-put-zach-miller-on-injured-reserve/ |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com}}</ref>

In 2018, Braunecker played in 15 games with two starts, recording three receptions for 42 yards and three [[special teams]] tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=February 7, 2019 |title=Bears 2018 position review: Tight end |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/bears-2018-position-review-tight-end |access-date=February 11, 2019 |publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]}}</ref>

On March 11, 2019, Braunecker signed a two-year contract extension with the Bears.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt, Darin |date=March 11, 2019 |title=Bears sign tight end Ben Braunecker |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/03/11/bears-sign-tight-end-ben-braunecker/ |access-date=March 14, 2026 |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> On November 10, 2019, he scored his first career NFL touchdown on an 18-yard touchdown pass from [[Mitchell Trubisky]] against the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref name="First career touchdown" /> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 15, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer, Larry |date=December 15, 2019 |title=Roster moves: Hicks activated, Braunecker to IR |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-hicks-activated-braunecker-to-ir |access-date=March 14, 2026 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref>

Braunecker was released by the Bears on July 23, 2020.<ref>{{cite news|last=Mayer|first=Larry|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-move-bears-release-ben-braunecker|title=Roster Move: Bears release Ben Braunecker|publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]|date=July 23, 2020|access-date=July 23, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Braunecker is married to former [[University of Notre Dame]] swimmer Sydney Golic; she is the daughter of former NFL player [[Mike Golic]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Hladik|first=Matt|url=https://thespun.com/more/sports-media/mike-golics-daughter-sydney-announces-engagement-to-nfl-player|title=Mike Golic's Daughter Sydney Announces Engagement To NFL Player|publisher=The Spun|date=July 20, 2020|access-date=July 20, 2020}}</ref>

'''Beau Benzschawel''' (born September 10, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin Badgers]] and signed with the [[Detroit Lions]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2019. He has also played for the [[Houston Texans]].

==Early life==
Benzschawel played [[tight end]] and [[defensive end]] on the [[high school football|football]] team at [[Grafton High School (Wisconsin)|Grafton High School]]. in addition, he played [[basketball]] and [[baseball]].<ref name="Commit">{{Cite web |last=Mulhern |first=Tom |date=October 25, 2013 |title=Badgers football: Grafton tight end-lineman Beau Benzschawel reverses field, commits for 2014 |url=http://host.madison.com/sports/college/football/badgers-football-grafton-tight-end-lineman-beau-benzschawel-reverses-field/article_0c170ea2-055e-5e94-80cf-be794512348b.html |access-date=May 18, 2018 |website=Madison.com}}</ref>

After originally committing to [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Potrykus |first=Jeff |date=October 24, 2013 |title=badgers get oral commitment from Grafton tight end Beau Benzschawel |url=http://archive.jsonline.com/blogs/sports/229141341.html |access-date=May 17, 2018 |website=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel}}</ref> Benzschawel committed to [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin]] on October 24, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosin |first=Andrew |date=October 24, 2013 |title=Beau Benzschawel becomes Badgers' 17th commit |url=https://www.buckys5thquarter.com/2013/10/24/4866066/wisconsin-badger-recruiting-grafton-wis-te-beau-benzschawel-becomes-badgers-17th-commitment-in-2014 |access-date=March 30, 2024 |website=Bucky's 5th Quarter |language=en}}</ref> He had other offers from [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State]], [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Wyoming]] and [[Bowling Green Falcons football|Bowling Green]], among others.<ref name="Commit" />

== College career ==
After redshirting the 2014 season, Benzschawel battled a knee injury before his redshirt freshman season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Galloway |first=Jason |date=August 17, 2015 |title=adgers football: Injuries pile up for UW's offensive line |url=http://draftbreakdown.com/2017/12/07/beau-benzschawel-vs-byu-2017/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104095604/http://draftbreakdown.com/2017/12/07/beau-benzschawel-vs-byu-2017/ |archive-date=January 4, 2018 |access-date=May 18, 2018 |website=The Journal Times}}</ref>

During his sophomore season, Benzschawel started every game at [[offensive guard]].<ref name="Preseason AA">{{Cite web |last=Potrykus |first=Jeff |date=August 29, 2017 |title=Beau Benzschawel knows postseason honors mean more than those in preseason |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uw/2017/08/29/beau-benzschawel-knows-postseason-honors-mean-more-than-those-preseason/610453001/ |access-date=May 16, 2018 |website=[[Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel]] |publisher=[[Gannett Company]]}}</ref>

Preceding his junior season, Benzschawel was named a pre-season All American by [[USA Today]].<ref name="Preseason AA" /> He injured his leg early in the season against [[Florida Atlantic Owls football|Florida Atlantic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Potrykus |first=Jeff |date=September 9, 2017 |title=Notes: UW guard Beau Benzschawel out with leg injury |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uw/2017/09/09/notes-uw-guard-beau-benzschawel-out-leg-injury/640028001/ |access-date=May 18, 2018 |website=Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel}}</ref> After being listed as questionable in the injury report for the following game,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pianovich |first=Stephen |title=Wisconsin's Jon Dietzen out, Beau Benzschawel questionable vs. BYU |url=https://www.landof10.com/wisconsin/wisconsin-football-jon-dietzen-beau-benzschawel-injury-byu |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180830004854/https://www.landof10.com/wisconsin/wisconsin-football-jon-dietzen-beau-benzschawel-injury-byu |archive-date=August 30, 2018 |access-date=May 18, 2018 |website=Land of 10}}</ref> he wound up playing against [[BYU Cougars football|BYU]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Matt |date=December 7, 2017 |title=Beau Benzschawel vs. BYU (2017) |url=http://draftbreakdown.com/2017/12/07/beau-benzschawel-vs-byu-2017/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104095604/http://draftbreakdown.com/2017/12/07/beau-benzschawel-vs-byu-2017/ |archive-date=January 4, 2018 |access-date=May 18, 2018 |website=Draft Breakdown}}</ref>

After the season, he was named a third-team All-American.<ref name="Orange Bowl">{{Cite web |last=Temple |first=Jesse |title=Wisconsin's All-America offensive linemen focused on Orange Bowl, not NFL Draft |url=https://www.landof10.com/wisconsin/wisconsin-american-offensive-linemen-focused-orange-bowl-not-nfl-draft-beau-benzschawel-michael-deiter-david-edwards |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180204071037/https://www.landof10.com/wisconsin/wisconsin-american-offensive-linemen-focused-orange-bowl-not-nfl-draft-beau-benzschawel-michael-deiter-david-edwards |archive-date=February 4, 2018 |access-date=May 16, 2018 |website=Land of 10}}</ref> He projected as a mid-round pick,<ref name="Orange Bowl" /> with reports highlighting his awareness and long arms.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dove |first=Jon |date=November 27, 2017 |title=Wisconsin's Beau Benzschawel NFL Draft Scouting Report |url=https://withthefirstpick.com/2017/11/27/beau-benzschawel-wisconsin-2018-nfl-draft-scouting-report/ |access-date=May 16, 2018 |website=With The First Pick |publisher=[[FanSided]]}}</ref> Eventually, he decided not to enter the [[2018 NFL draft]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenstein |first=Teddy |date=February 25, 2018 |title=Wisconsin offensive linemen hunger for more success after turning down NFL cash |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-wisconsin-offensive-line-nfl-draft-20180225-story.html |access-date=May 16, 2018 |website=[[Chicago Tribune]]}}</ref> after consulting with the NFL Draft Advisory Board.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Galloway |first=Jason |date=December 31, 2017 |title=Badgers football: Nick Nelson to enter NFL draft, Beau Benzschawel to stay at Wisconsin for senior season |url=http://host.madison.com/wsj/sports/college/football/badgers-football-nick-nelson-to-enter-nfl-draft-beau-benzschawel/article_60fe1e89-4268-5503-843a-a94df0903a3d.html |access-date=May 16, 2018 |website=[[Wisconsin State Journal]]}}</ref>

In August 2018, Benzschawel was named a preseason second-team All-America by CBS Sports.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Silverstein |first=Adam |date=August 15, 2018 |title=2018 CBS Sports Preseason All-America team: College football's best and brightest |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/2018-cbs-sports-preseason-all-america-team-college-footballs-best-and-brightest/ |access-date=August 15, 2018 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>  He was also named a preseason first-team All-American by USA Today<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 21, 2018 |title=USA TODAY Sports' preseason college football All-America team |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/2018/08/21/usa-today-sports-college-football-preseason-all-america-team/979463002/ |access-date=August 31, 2018 |website=USA Today}}</ref> and the Associated Press.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 21, 2018 |title=AP 2018 Preseason All-America Team, List |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/2018/08/21/ap-2018-preseason-all-america-team-list/37553273/ |access-date=March 30, 2024 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> At the end of the season, Benzschawel was named a Consensus All-American.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kocorowski |first=Jake |date=December 12, 2018 |title=Jonathan Taylor claims unanimous All-American honors |url=https://www.buckys5thquarter.com/2018/12/12/18138101/wisconsin-football-jonathan-taylor-unanimous-all-american-beau-benzschawel |website=Bucky's 5th Quarter}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Alan Braden''' (born March 9, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]]. He is currently the fueler for the number 66 [[Meyer Shank Racing]] entry in the [[Indycar Series]].

==Early life==
Braden was born on March 9, 1994 in Rockford, Michigan.<ref name="U-M OL B. Braden">[https://mgoblue.com/sports/football/roster/ben-braden/1390 "Michigan Wolverines"] Profile. Retrieved November 7, 2024.</ref> From an early age, Braden played hockey intending to play professionally as a [[goaltender|goalie]]. He admired [[Czech Republic|Czech]] [[ice hockey]] player [[Dominik Hasek]]. By the time Braden began junior high school, he settled on playing football.<ref name="U-M OL Ben Braden">Snyder, Mark (November 11, 2015). [https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2015/11/11/wolverines-main/75630804/ "Detroit Free Press: 'U-M offensive lineman Braden learning to dominate'"]. Detroit Free Press. Retrieved November 7, 2024.</ref> Braden played as a [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|tackle]] with the Rockford Rams, including at starting right tackle during his sophomore and junior seasons in 2010 and 2011. During his senior season in 2012, Braden was named to the AP Michigan all-state first team. The Detroit Free Press named Braden to the Detroit News Blue Chip List. He was rated a three-star recruit by [[247Sports]]. Braden earned three letters during his freshman, sophomore and junior seasons.<ref name="U-M OL B. Braden"/> This led to four offers from [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin]], [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse]], [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State]] and [[University of Michigan|Michigan]].<ref name="Rockford Rams OT Ben Braden">[https://247sports.com/Player/Ben-Braden-10982/high-school-11233/ "247Sports"] Recruitment Profile. Retrieved November 7, 2024.</ref>

==College career==
Braden committed to Michigan, [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] the 2012 season. During the 2013 season, Braden earned his first varsity letter despite only appearing in two games as a reserve [[offensive lineman]]. In his junior season in 2014, Braden started in all 12 games, playing as a right tackle. His performance earned him a second letter. During his senior season in 2015, Braden was assigned guard position and started in all 13 games. His senior season saw him earn his third varsity letter. During his final season in 2016, Braden played left guard in four games. He later started 7 games at left tackle, earning All-Big Ten second team honors. He graduated in 2016 with a degree in [[general studies]].<ref name="U-M OL B. Braden"/>

'''Benjamin Gerald Bordelon''' (born April 9, 1974) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] for the [[San Diego Chargers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) in 1997. He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]], [[starting lineup|starting]] for four seasons as an [[offensive guard]] and tackle and earning second-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] honors as a senior in 1996.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Bordelon Bio |url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=204967406 |website=LSUsports.net |publisher=Louisiana State University |access-date=September 22, 2018 |archive-date=September 22, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922211838/http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=204967406 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Since 2014, Bordelon has been president, chairman, and chief executive officer of [[Bollinger Shipyards]]. He has been chief operating officer since 2013 and a board member since 2002. Bordelon is a grandson of Bollinger founder [[Donald G. Bollinger]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Griggs |first1=Ted |title=Bollinger Shipyards sold to third-generation Bollinger executive, Chouest family |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/news/business/article_2850f2c9-dcad-5c1d-a0dd-2e1e0341d039.html |access-date=September 22, 2018 |work=The Advocate |date=January 3, 2015}}</ref>

'''Ben Burr-Kirven''' (born September 8, 1997) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] who played for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Washington Huskies football|Washington Huskies]].

==Early life==
Burr-Kirven attended [[Sacred Heart Preparatory (Atherton, California)|Sacred Heart Preparatory School]] in [[Atherton, California]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stephens |first=Mitch |date=October 6, 2017 |title=Sacred Heart Prep-Atherton alum Ben Burr-Kirven thriving with Washington |url=https://www.sfgate.com/sharks/article/Sacred-Heart-Prep-Atherton-alum-Ben-Burr-Kirven-12256761.php |access-date=May 18, 2023 |website=SFGate}}</ref> He was the ''[[San Jose Mercury News]]'' Player of the Year as a junior and senior.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Milles |first=Todd |date=August 12, 2017 |title=Washington Huskies linebacker Ben Burr-Kirven has resume, but not much playing time |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2017/aug/12/washington-huskies-linebacker-ben-burr-kirven-has-/ |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=The Spokesman-Review}}</ref> He committed to the [[University of Washington]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sabedra |first=Darren  |date=2014-09-18 |title=Football: Sacred Heart Prep's Ben Burr-Kirven commits to Washington |url=https://blogs.mercurynews.com/hssports/2014/09/18/football-sacred-heart-preps-ben-burr-kirven-commits-to-washington/ |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=Varsity Extra |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Burr-Kirven played at Washington from 2015 to 2018. He became a starter during his junior season in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clark |first=Ryan S. |date=October 31, 2017 |title=Once deemed too small, Burr-Kirven plays big role for Huskies |url=https://www.theolympian.com/sports/college/pac-12/university-of-washington/article181936041.html |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=The Olympian}}</ref> As a senior in 2018, he was the [[Pac-12 Conference]] Defensive Player of the Year and a member of the [[Associated Press]] [[All-America]] team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Husky linebacker Ben Burr-Kirven named Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/college/pac-12/university-of-washington/article222638665.html |website=thenewstribune}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jude |first=Adam |date=December 6, 2018 |title=Washington star linebacker Ben Burr-Kirven drawing increased attention from NFL scouts |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-football/washington-star-linebacker-ben-burr-kirven-drawing-increased-attention-from-nfl-scouts/ |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=The Seattle Times}}</ref> He majored in [[film studies]] at Washington, and received honors from the department.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 5, 2018 |title=Student Spotlight: Ben Burr-Kirven | url=https://cinema.washington.edu/news/2018/03/05/student-spotlight-ben-burr-kirven |website=Department of Cinema & Media Studies, University of Washington}}</ref>

Burr-Kirven was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the fifth round (142nd overall) of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=April 27, 2019 |title=Seahawks Select Washington Linebacker Ben Burr-Kirven No. 142 Overall In 2019 NFL Draft |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-select-university-of-washington-linebacker-ben-burr-kirven-in-fifth-rou |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> As a rookie, he appeared in 16 games. Burr-Kirven was placed on [[injured reserve]] on August 23, 2021, after suffering a [[torn ACL]] in the preseason.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=August 23, 2021 |title=Seahawks Place Two On Injured Reserve, Waive Two To Reduce Roster To 80 |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-place-two-on-injured-reserve-waive-two-to-reduce-roster-to-80 |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was waived on July 26, 2022, and placed on the reserve/[[physically unable to perform]] list.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=July 26, 2022 |title=Seahawks Waive Ben Burr-Kirven With Failed Physical Designation; Place Four On PUP List |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-waive-ben-burr-kirven-with-failed-physical-designation-place-four-on-pu |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

On March 10, 2023, Burr-Kirven was released by the Seahawks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=March 10, 2023 |title=Seahawks Release G Gabe Jackson & LB Ben Burr-Kirven |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-release-g-gabe-jackson-lb-ben-burr-kirven |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was re-signed by the Seahawks on July 27.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=July 27, 2023 |title=Seahawks Sign LB Ben Burr-Kirven |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-lb-ben-burr-kirven |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was released on August 29.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Seahawks Make Roster Moves, Establish Initial 2023 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-establish-initial-2023-53-man-roster |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

'''Bashir Jihad Yamini''' (born September 10, 1977) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played for the [[Tennessee Titans]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/Y/YamiBa20.htm |title=Bashir Yamini Stats |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com |date= |access-date=February 28, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/bashiryamini/2503932/profile |title=Bashir Yamini, WR |work=Nfl.com |date= |access-date=February 28, 2020}}</ref>

==Biography==
Yamini was an accomplished track and field athlete at the [[University of Iowa]] from 1996-1999. Competing for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes track and field]] team, Yamini won the 1998 [[long jump at the NCAA Division I Indoor Track and Field Championships]] with a jump of 7.93 meters.<ref>{{cite web |title=Five Hawkeyes named to 2012 Hall of Fame Class |url=https://now.uiowa.edu/news/2012/06/five-hawkeyes-named-2012-hall-fame-class |access-date=18 June 2024}}</ref> He played football for the Hawkeyes from 1997-1999. He didn’t make a catch in 1997. In the 1998 season, he finished the year with 31 receptions for 317 yards and no touchdowns. In the 1999 season, he finished with 26 receptions for 348 yards and one touchdown.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bashir Yamini|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bashir-yamini-1.html|website=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref>

Yamini was signed on April 17, 2000, by the [[Denver Broncos]] after going undrafted in the [[2000 NFL draft]]. He was waived by the Broncos and then acquired by the [[Tennessee Titans]] on August 29, 2000. He only appeared in six games that season, and wasn’t a starter. He was targeted once throughout the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=BASHIR YAMINI|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playery/yami00100.html|website=ProFootballArchives.com|access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref> He also played for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and the [[Carolina Panthers]], but never in a regular season game for either team. He had a brief stint with the [[Ottawa Renegades]] in 2004 and was signed again on February 10, 2005.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ruiz, Renegades reach terms|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/football/ruiz-renegades-reach-terms-1.561717|website=CBC.ca|date=February 10, 2005|access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref> He was released by the Renegades as a part of their final roster cuts on June 18, 2005.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fina Cuts Today|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2005/06/18/final_cuts_today/|website=CFL.ca|date=June 18, 2005|access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref>
