'''Benjamin Bartch''' (born July 22, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (American football)|guard]] for the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Saint John's Johnnies football|Saint John's Johnnies]] and was selected in the fourth round of the [[2020 NFL draft]] by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].

==Early life==
Bartch grew up in [[McMinnville, Oregon]], and attended [[Blanchet Catholic School]] where he played [[wide receiver|receiver]], [[tight end]], and [[linebacker]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crepea |first=James |date=February 28, 2020 |title=Dayton's Ben Bartch vying to go from Division 3 St. John's (Minn.) to NFL |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/collegefootball/2020/02/daytons-ben-bartch-vying-to-go-from-division-3-st-johns-minn-to-nfl.html |access-date=April 7, 2020 |work=[[The Oregonian]]}}</ref> Although he was tall, Bartch was also very skinny and was primarily a backup receiver for Blanchet, not yet discovered for his blocking abilities; as a senior, Bartch was billed at 195 pounds and only a recorded a handful of receptions and tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Bartch, Maxpreps |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/or/salem/blanchet-catholic-cavaliers/athletes/ben-bartch/?careerid=r6nhtmpjaseee}}</ref> He was not recruited after high school and chose to play at [[Saint John's University (Minnesota)|Saint John's University]], a [[NCAA Division III|Division III]] program. He was also a 4-year letterer in basketball at Blanchet.

==College career==
Bartch began his collegiate career playing tight end. Entering Saint John's, Bartch was billed at 220 pounds, appearing in one game as a freshman. As a sophomore, Bartch was the team's third-string tight end, catching four passes for 43 yards and one touchdown, mostly contributing to [[special teams]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Auman |first=Greg |date=February 26, 2020 |title=Tight end-turned-O-lineman Ben Bartch goes from 250 to 309, from Div. III to NFL |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1637203/2020/02/26/tight-end-turned-o-lineman-ben-bartch-goes-from-250-to-309-from-div-iii-to-nfl/ |access-date=April 7, 2020 |work=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref>

His coaches noticed his blocking ability, with one calling it "a hidden natural-born talent" and suggested he move to the offensive line going into his junior season. In order to gain weight, Bartch consumed a protein shake daily consisting of 7 scrambled eggs, a tub of cottage cheese, quick grits, peanut butter, bananas, and [[Gatorade]], growing from 240 pounds to 275 in just the summer. He eventually reached 308 pounds with this method.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Gartland |first=Dan |date=February 27, 2020 |title=D-III Draft Prospect Ben Bartch Drank an Unholy Concoction to Pack on 60 Pounds |url=https://www.si.com/extra-mustard/2020/02/27/nfl-draft-ben-bartch-protein-shake-weight-gain |access-date=April 7, 2020 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Labbe |first=Dan |date=February 26, 2020 |title=How offensive lineman Ben Bartch used a gag-inducing smoothie and YouTube to reach the NFL combine |url=https://www.cleveland.com/browns/2020/02/how-offensive-lineman-ben-bartch-used-a-magic-shake-and-youtube-to-make-it-to-the-nfl-combine.html |access-date=April 7, 2020 |website=[[Cleveland.com]]}}</ref> Bartch became the Johnnies starting left tackle and was named second-team All-[[Minnesota Intercollegiate Athletic Conference]] (MIAC) and to the [[Allstate]] [[American Football Coaches Association|AFCA]] Good Works Team at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 12, 2019 |title=Bartch, Munoz named to Allstate AFCA Good Works Team |url=https://www.miacathletics.com/sports/fball/2019-20/releases/20190912wwz2ps |access-date=April 7, 2020 |website=MIACAthletics.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2019 |title=On eve of season opener, pro scouts eye Johnnies' quarterback, offensive lineman |url=https://www.sctimes.com/story/sports/2019/09/06/st-johns-football-johnnies-schedule-ncaa-nfl-draft-scouts/2225676001/ |access-date=April 7, 2020 |work=[[St. Cloud Times]]}}</ref> As a senior, Bartch was named first-team All-MIAC and a consensus first-team [[All-American]] by D3Football.com, as well as second-team All-American by the [[Associated Press]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 31, 2020 |title=St. John's tackle Ben Bartch measures up against the best at Senior Bowl |url=https://www.startribune.com/st-john-s-tackle-ben-bartch-measures-up-agianst-the-best-at-senior-bowl/567445782/ |access-date=April 7, 2020 |work=[[Star Tribune]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Russo |first1=Ralph |title=North Central highlights AP Division III All-America Team |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2019/12/19/north-central-highlights-ap-division-iii-all-america-team/ |website=San Diego Union Tribune |publisher=The San Diego Union-Tribune |access-date=25 March 2026}}</ref> Considered a prospect in the [[2020 NFL draft]], Bartch was invited to participate in the [[2020 Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Melo |first=Justin |date=February 18, 2020 |title=Meet Ben Bartch, the latest small-school Senior Bowl star |url=https://draftwire.usatoday.com/2020/02/18/2020-nfl-draft-prospects-ben-bartch-interview/ |access-date=April 7, 2020 |work=Draft Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> A rival coach wrote that Ben Bartch was "the best D3 player I had ever seen" and that he was "by far the best player on that team" despite playing alongside two [[Power Five conferences|Power Five]] transfers at Saint John's, including a quarterback from [[Penn State Nittany Lions|Penn State]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Post Draft Q&A: An offensive line coach explains Ben Bartch's potential with the Jaguars |url=https://www.bigcatcountry.com/2020/5/6/21249122/post-draft-q-a-offensive-line-coach-explains-ben-bartch-potential-jacksonville-jaguars |work=Big Cat Country|date=May 6, 2020}}</ref>

Bartch also competed on Saint John's track and field team in [[shot put]] and [[discus throw]] events.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 6, 2020 |title=Ben Bartch could be the Redskins' answer at LT |url=https://www.hogshaven.com/2020/4/6/21208814/ben-bartch-could-be-the-redskins-answer-at-lt |access-date=April 7, 2020 |website=HogsHaven.com |publisher=[[SB Nation]]}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On November 21, 2023, Bartch was signed by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] to their active roster off of the Jaguars' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 21, 2023 |title=49ers Sign OL Bartch; Place S Hufanga on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-offensive-lineman-ben-bartch-safety-talanoa-hufanga-injured-reserve |access-date=November 21, 2023 |publisher=49ers.com}}</ref> On December 12, 2024, Bartch was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Activate Dre Greenlaw from the Reserve/PUP list and Place OL Ben Bartch on IR|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-activate-dre-greenlaw-from-the-reserve-pup-list-and-place-ol-ben-bartch-on-ir|website=49ers.com|date=December 12, 2024|access-date=December 12, 2024}}</ref>

On February 24, 2025, Bartch signed a one-year contract extension with the 49ers.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Sign Offensive Lineman Ben Bartch to One-Year Extension|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-offensive-lineman-ben-bartch-to-one-year-extension|website=49ers.com|date=February 24, 2025|access-date=February 25, 2025}}</ref> On September 17, Bartch was placed on injured reserve, having suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 2 against the [[2025 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web |title=49ers Place OL Bartch on IR, Promote TE Willis to Roster, Other Roster Moves |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-place-ol-bartch-on-ir-promote-te-willis-to-roster-other-roster-moves |website=49ers.com |date=17 September 2025 |access-date=18 September 2025}}</ref> On November 8, Bartch was activated ahead of the 49ers' Week 10 matchup against the [[2025 Los Angeles Rams season|Los Angeles Rams]].<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Activate Ben Bartch, Make Roster Moves Ahead of Week 10|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-activate-ben-bartch-make-roster-moves-ahead-of-week-10|website=49ers.com|date=November 8, 2025|access-date=November 8, 2025}}</ref> On December 8, Bartch was placed back on injured reserve after suffering a significant foot sprain in Week 13 against the [[2025 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Place OL Ben Bartch on IR, Claim LB Garret Wallow from Broncos|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-place-ol-ben-bartch-on-ir-claim-lb-garret-wallow-from-broncos|website=49ers.com|date=December 8, 2025|access-date=December 9, 2025}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
Cleveland was selected in the third round with the 94th overall pick of the [[2021 NFL draft]] by the [[Baltimore Ravens]]. The Ravens obtained the 94th overall pick as part of the trade that sent [[Orlando Brown Jr.]] to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Select Ben Cleveland With 94th Pick|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ben-cleveland-nfl-draft-guard-georgia|author=Brown, Clifton|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=May 1, 2021}}</ref> On July 20, 2021, Cleveland signed his four-year rookie contract worth $4.8 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/bs-sp-ravens-nfl-draft-ben-cleveland-20210501-4bmulehfezbajniptaj7hpucji-story.html|title=Ravens take powerful Georgia guard Ben Cleveland with third-round pick, No. 94 overall|work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|date=May 1, 2020|access-date=May 3, 2021}}</ref> He was placed on the active/[[non-football injury list]] at the start of training camp on July 21.<ref>{{cite news |author=Shaffer, Jonas |title=Ravens place G Ben Cleveland, TE Jake Breeland on nonfootball injury list |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/bs-sp-ravens-ben-cleveland-nfi-20210721-kfpbiqhqzzd2np47vk63quobsu-story.html |website=BaltimoreSun.com |date=July 21, 2021 |access-date=July 22, 2021}}</ref> On October 12, Cleveland suffered a knee injury in Week 5 against the [[Indianapolis Colts]] and was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ben Cleveland Placed on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ben-cleveland-placed-on-injured-reserve|author=Brown, Clifton|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=October 12, 2021}}</ref> On November 20, Cleveland was activated to the active roster from [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ben Cleveland Activated to 53-Man Roster, Pernell McPhee to Injured Reserve|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ben-cleveland-activated-to-53-man-roster-pernell-mcphee-to-injured-reserve|author=Brown, Clifton|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=November 20, 2021}}</ref>

In Week 6 of the 2024 season against the [[Washington Commanders]], Cleveland blocked a field goal attempt by [[Austin Seibert]]. The Ravens went on to win the game 30–23.<ref>{{cite web |title=Washington Commanders at Baltimore Ravens - October 13th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202410130rav.htm |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |access-date=19 October 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

On March 15, 2025, Cleveland re-signed with the Ravens.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Re-Sign Offensive Lineman Ben Cleveland|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ben-cleveland-ravens-free-agency-resign-guard-2024|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=March 15, 2025}}</ref> On December 8, Cleveland was suspended for three games for violating the NFL's substance abuse policy.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ravens guard Ben Cleveland suspended 3 games for violating NFL’s Substances Abuse Policy|url=https://foxbaltimore.com/sports/sports-unlimited/ravens-guard-ben-cleveland-suspended-three-games|date=December 8, 2025|website=Fox 45}}</ref> On January 1, 2026, Cleveland was waived by the Ravens following his suspension.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Erby |first=Glenn |title=Baltimore Ravens waive Ben Cleveland following a three-game suspension |url=https://ravenswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/ravens/2026/01/01/baltimore-ravens-waive-ben-cleveland/87985876007/ |access-date=2026-01-01 |website=Ravens Wire |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On January 5, 2026, Cleveland was signed to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers sign offensive lineman to practice squad ahead of playoffs|url=https://chargerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/chargers/2026/01/05/chargers-roster-playoffs-ben-cleveland/88036697007/|work=Chargers Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=January 5, 2026}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 14.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Signed G Ben Cleveland To Futures Deal|url=https://nfltraderumors.co/chargers-signed-g-ben-cleveland-to-futures-deal/|work=NFL Trade Rumors|date=January 14, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On February 12, 2025, Cleveland was arrested by the [[Baldwin County, Georgia|Baldwin County]] Sheriff’s Office for DUI and failure to maintain lane. According to authorities, Cleveland blew a .178 on a breathalyzer test.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ravens OL Ben Cleveland arrested, cited for DUI on Feb. 12|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ravens-ol-ben-cleveland-arrested-cited-for-dui-on-feb-12|access-date=February 17, 2025|website=nfl.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Ben Anthony "Honey Buns" Cavil''' (born January 31, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] for two seasons with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]]. In addition to Baltimore, Cavil played professionally with the [[San Diego Chargers]], [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Scottish Claymores]] and [[New York/New Jersey Hitmen]].

==Early life and education==
Ben Cavil was born on January 31, 1972, in [[Galveston, Texas]]. He attended high school at [[La Marque High School|La Marque (TX)]]. Cavil then went to college and played football for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ben Cavil - SoonerStats - Historical scores, records, and stats for Oklahoma Sooners football, basketball, baseball, and softball|url=http://soonerstats.com/football/players/details.cfm?playerid=287|access-date=May 10, 2021|website=soonerstats.com}}</ref> He lettered from 1991 to 1994 before being signed by the [[San Diego Chargers]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerc/cavi00200.html|title=Ben Cavil Stats - Pro Football Archives|website=www.profootballarchives.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===San Diego Chargers===
Cavil went undrafted in the [[1995 NFL draft]] and was then signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[San Diego Chargers]]. He dislocated his wrist in training camp and was subsequently placed on injured reserve, ending his season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/77462394/the-baltimore-sun/|newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 12, 1997|title=Cavil gives offensive line a boost in his backup role|access-date=May 10, 2021}} {{Open access}}</ref> He did not make the roster in his second season.

===Philadelphia Eagles===
After being released by San Diego, Cavil was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He would be released at roster cuts but later signed to the practice squad, where he stayed all season. He was traded to the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in exchange for a 7th round draft pick the next year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CaviBe20.htm|title=Ben Cavil Stats|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/77461963/the-news-journal/|newspaper=[[The News Journal]]|date=August 25, 1997|title=Ravens boost offensive line|access-date=May 10, 2021|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
After being traded, Cavil was able to make the roster of Baltimore.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/77463699/the-baltimore-sun/|newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|date=July 28, 1998|access-date=May 10, 2021|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|title=Once more, it's all over for Isaia|author=Lambrecht, Gary}} {{Open access}}</ref> He would then make an appearance in 15 out of 16 games, missing only the final week.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CaviBe20.htm|title=Ben Cavil 1997 Game Log|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He started 8 of those games. He had 4 penalties in the season. The next year Cavil came back and appeared in all 16 games, but only starting 6.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CaviBe20.htm|title=Ben Cavil 1998 Game Log|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> Cavil was nicknamed "Honey Buns" by Ravens teammates. He would leave the Ravens the next year after being drafted in the [[1999 NFL expansion draft]].

===Cleveland Browns===
Cavil was then selected in the [[1999 NFL expansion draft]] by the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/77462291/telegraph-forum/|newspaper=[[Telegraph-Fornum]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=February 10, 1999|access-date=May 10, 2021|title=Capsule looks at the players taken in the draft}} {{Open access}}</ref> He was released at roster cuts.

===Scottish Claymores===
In 2000, Cavil played for the [[Scottish Claymores]] of [[NFL Europe]].<ref name="auto"/>

===New York/New Jersey Hitmen===
His final season was in 2001 with the [[New York/New Jersey Hitmen]] of the [[XFL (2001)|XFL]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=NY/NJ Hitmen Roster: Ben Cavil|url=http://www.all-xfl.com/nynjhitmen/team/roster/bencavil.htm|access-date=May 10, 2021|website=www.all-xfl.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
After his professional career Cavil worked in real estate.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/77459960/the-baltimore-sun/|newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|access-date=May 10, 2021|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|author=Klingaman, Mike|date=December 7, 2007|title=At home}} {{Open access}}</ref> He also enjoyed collecting [[comic book]]s.<ref name="auto1"/>

'''Baylon Spector''' (born October 20, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]]. He was drafted by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the seventh round of the [[2022 NFL draft]]. 

==College career==
Spector was a member of the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] for five seasons and [[redshirted]] his true freshman season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keepfer |first=Scott |date=January 1, 2021 |title=3 things to know about Clemson linebacker Baylon Spector |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2021/01/01/baylon-spector-clemson-tigers-football-linebacker-facts-sugar-bowl/4106751001/ |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=[[The Greenville News]]}}</ref> He was named a starter at weak side linebacker going into his redshirt junior season and was named All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] by the [[Associated Press]] after leading the team with 72 tackles and 4.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cubit |first=Alexis |date=June 25, 2021 |title=Skalski, Spector highlight Clemson's strong linebacker group |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article252364203.html |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]}}</ref> As a redshirt senior Spector was the Tigers' second-leading tackler with 85.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keepfer |first=Scott |date=May 1, 2022 |title=Pros and cons of the Bills drafting Clemson football's Baylon Spector in 2022 NFL Draft |url=https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/2022/04/30/baylon-spector-nfl-draft-2022-clemson-football-buffalo-bills/7368837001/ |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=[[Anderson Independent Mail]]}}</ref> Spector finished his college career with  210 tackles, 22.0 tackles for loss, 9.0 sacks, four forced fumbles, four fumble recoveries, and a one interception in 53 games played with 21 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Summers |first=Todd |date=April 30, 2022 |title=Clemson LB Baylon Spector selected by the Bills in the 7th round |url=https://www.wspa.com/sports/clemson-tigers-sports/clemson-lb-baylon-spector-selected-by-the-bills-in-the-7th-round/ |access-date=May 2, 2022 |website=[[WSPA-TV|WSPA.com]]}}</ref>

'''Beaux Limmer''' (born June 10, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for the [[Los Angeles Rams]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas Razorbacks]].

==Early life==
Limmer was born on June 10, 2001 in Tyler, Texas,{{citation needed|date=April 2024}} the son of David and Susan Limmer. He attended [[Tyler Legacy High School|Robert E. Lee High School]] in Tyler.<ref name=Bio>{{cite web|title=Beaux Limmer|date=June 19, 2019 |publisher=University of Arkansas|accessdate=August 31, 2023|url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/beaux-limmer/}}</ref>

==College football==
Limmer enrolled at the [[University of Arkansas]] in 2019. As a redshirt sophomore in 2021, he started the last 11 games for the Razorbacks. As a redshirt junior in 2022, he started all 13 games, the first 12 at right guard before switching to center for the Liberty Bowl. He was selected by [[Pro Football Focus]] as a third-team All-American.<ref name=Bio/>

A video of Limmer squatting 700 pounds went viral in the summer of 2023.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Fuller |first=Jackson  |date=August 4, 2023 |title=700-pound squat? Arkansas football's Beaux Limmer could have lifted more |url=https://www.swtimes.com/story/sports/2023/08/04/700-pound-squat-not-the-max-for-arkansas-footballs-beaux-limmer/70528657007/ |access-date=2024-07-04 |work=Fort Smith Southwest Times Record}}</ref> In August 2023, Pro Football Focus ranked Limmer at No. 27 on its list of the 50 best players in college football.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chadwick |first=Max  |date=August 4, 2023 |title=PFF College 50: The 50 best players in college football right now |url=https://www.pff.com/news/college-football-pff-college-50-the-50-best-players-in-college-football-right-now |access-date=2024-07-04 |publisher=Pro Football Focus}}</ref>

Limmer moved to the center position for Arkansas in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Choate |first=Mason  |date=April 14, 2023 |title=Beaux Limmer still adjusting to center with Arkansas |url=https://arkansas.rivals.com/news/beaux-limmer-still-adjusting-to-center-with-arkansas |access-date=2024-07-04 |website=HawgBeat.com |publisher=Rivals.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Priddy |first=Drake  |date=August 15, 2023 |title=Beaux Limmer making full transition to center |url=https://www.nwahomepage.com/sports/pig-trail-nation/beaux-limmer-making-full-transition-to-center/ |access-date=2024-07-04 |publisher=Pig Trail Nation}}</ref> Prior to the 2023 season, he was also named to the watch lists for the [[Outland Trophy|Outland]] and [[Rimington Trophy|Rimington Trophies]].<ref name=Bio/>

'''Timothy Benjamin Brown''' (born May 19, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]] and has also been a member of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].

==Early life==
Brown was born on May 19, 1998.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrowBe01.htm|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Ben Brown Stats}}</ref> He attended [[Vicksburg Catholic School|St. Aloysius High School]] in [[Vicksburg, Mississippi]], where he played [[offensive tackle]] and [[defensive tackle]] and earned first-team all-state honors, as well as second-team [[All-American]] honors, as a [[Senior (education)|senior]] while compiling 37 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] and a [[Quarterback sack|sack]] and helping St. Aloysius gain 2,596 rushing yards with an average 7.2 yards-per-carry.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballnetwork.com/ben-brown-ole-miss-og-nfl-draft-scouting-report-2022/|publisher=Pro Football Network|title=Ben Brown, Ole Miss OG {{!}} NFL Draft Scouting Report|author=Hodkinson, Oliver|date=July 8, 2021}}</ref>

Ranked a three-star recruit, Brown committed to play [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/ole-miss/2016/02/23/three-star-brown-commits-ole-miss/80829284/|newspaper=[[The Clarion-Ledger]]|title=Three-star Ben Brown: Incredible to commit to Rebels|date=February 23, 2016|author=Paulling, Daniel}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true [[freshman]] at Ole Miss in 2017, Brown [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vicksburgpost.com/2018/08/08/former-st-al-star-brown-pushing-for-starting-spot-on-ole-miss-o-line/|newspaper=[[The Vicksburg Post]]|title=Former St. Al star Brown pushing for starting spot on Ole Miss' O-line|date=August 8, 2018}}</ref> The following year, he became a starter at [[right guard]] and started every game, not allowing any [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] on 446 pass plays while earning [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman honors while being one of three freshmen nationally to start every game at his position.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vicksburgpost.com/2018/12/07/ole-miss-lineman-vicksburg-native-brown-on-freshman-all-sec-team/|newspaper=[[The Vicksburg Post]]|title=Ole Miss lineman, Vicksburg native Brown on Freshman All-SEC team|date=December 7, 2018}}</ref> In 2019, Brown started all 12 games, allowing only one sack, while playing a total of 765 snaps at offensive guard and 99 at [[Center (gridiron football)|center]].<ref name="auto"/>

Brown transitioned to being a center full-time in 2020 and started all 10 games, being named to the watchlist for the [[Rimington Trophy]] as best center nationally.<ref name="auto"/> He continued starting as a senior in 2021, but ended up missing the final half of the year after tearing his [[biceps]] in the final minutes of Ole Miss' game against [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/ole-miss/2021/10/26/ole-miss-football-rebels-ben-brown-surgery-injury-offensive-line/8561485002/|newspaper=[[The Clarion-Ledger]]|title=Ole Miss senior offensive lineman Ben Brown out for season, ending career|date=October 26, 2021|author=Suss, Nick}}</ref> He finished his collegiate career having started 40 consecutive games.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vicksburgpost.com/2022/04/24/former-ole-miss-st-al-star-ben-brown-hoping-to-hear-name-called-in-nfl-draft/|newspaper=[[The Vicksburg Post]]|title=Former Ole Miss, St. Al star Ben Brown hoping to hear name called in NFL draft|author=Bowker, Ernest|date=April 24, 2022}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
Brown had been commonly projected to be a fifth-to-sixth round pick in the [[2022 NFL draft]] prior to his injury, but afterwards went unselected.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.on3.com/teams/ole-miss-rebels/news/adding-value-ben-browns-versatility-is-his-greatest-strength-as-he-vies-to-make-the-cincinnati-bengals/|website=On3.com|title=Adding Value: Ben Brown's versatility is his greatest strength as he vies to make the Cincinnati Bengals|author=Garrett, Ben|date=May 3, 2022}}</ref> He signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] as an [[Free agent#Undrafted free agent|undrafted free agent]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://bengalswire.usatoday.com/2022/04/30/bengals-undrafted-free-agent-profile-ole-miss-ben-brown/|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|title=Bengals undrafted free agent profile: Ole Miss G/C Ben Brown|author=Roling, Chris|date=April 30, 2022}}</ref> He injured his biceps in the first preseason game and was placed on [[injured reserve]], ending his first season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vicksburgpost.com/2022/08/15/bengals-put-vicksburg-native-ben-brown-on-injured-reserve/|newspaper=[[The Vicksburg Post]]|title=Bengals put Vicksburg native Ben Brown on injured reserve|date=August 15, 2022}}</ref> The following season, he was released at the final roster cuts on August 29, 2023.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://vicksburgnews.com/ben-brown-released-by-the-bengals/|newspaper=[[Vicksburg Daily News]]|author=Phillips, Keith|date=August 29, 2023|title=Ben Brown released by the Bengals}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
Two days after being released by Cincinnati, Brown was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vicksburgpost.com/2023/09/01/vicksburg-native-ben-brown-signs-with-seahawks/|newspaper=[[The Vicksburg Post]]|title=Vicksburg native Ben Brown signs with Seahawks|author=Bowker, Ernest|date=September 1, 2023}}</ref> He was signed to the active roster on September 4.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://seahawkswire.usatoday.com/lists/seahawks-announce-5-roster-moves-before-first-week-1-practice/|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|title=Seahawks announce 5 roster moves before first Week 1 practice|date=September 4, 2023|author=Weaver, Tim}}</ref> He was waived on October 21, 2023 and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign C Joey Hunt, Elevate Two From Practice Squad|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-c-joey-hunt-elevate-two-from-practice-squad|website=Seahawks.com|date=October 21, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Tony |title=Seahawks Re-Sign OL Ben Brown To PS |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/seahawks-re-sign-ol-ben-brown-to-ps/ |website=NFL Trade Rumors |access-date=25 October 2023}}</ref> He was released on November 26.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign CB Kelvin Joseph & WR Cody White To Practice Squad|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-cb-kelvin-joseph-wr-cody-white-to-practice-squad|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=November 26, 2023}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On January 1, 2024, Brown was signed to the [[Arizona Cardinals]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Arizona Cardinals sign offensive lineman Ben Brown to practice squad|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/3540642/arizona-cardinals-sign-offensive-lineman-ben-brown-to-practice-squad/|work=Arizona Sports|date=January 1, 2024}}</ref> He was not signed to a reserve/future contract after the season, and thus became a free agent upon the expiration of his practice squad contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/cardinals/news/arizona-cardinals-sign-12-players-future-contracts|website=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Cardinals Sign 12 Players to Future Contracts|date=January 10, 2024|author=Druin, Donnie}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On January 16, 2024, Brown signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders announce 3 Reserve/Future signings|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-3-reserve-future-signings-nfl-2024-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=January 16, 2024}}</ref> He was waived on August 27, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders make moves to bring roster to 53-player limit|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-make-moves-to-bring-roster-to-53-man-roster-nfl-2024-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders announce practice squad additions|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-practice-squad-additions-nfl-roster-2024-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=August 28, 2024}}</ref>

=== New England Patriots ===
On October 10, 2024, Brown was signed to the [[New England Patriots]]' active roster off the Raiders practice squad.<ref>{{cite web | last=Alper | first=Josh | title=OL Ben Brown signs two-year extension with the Patriots | website=NBC Sports | date=2025-12-23 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/ol-ben-brown-signs-two-year-extension-with-the-patriots | access-date=2026-04-23}}</ref> He made his first NFL career start at center, in Week 6 against the [[2025 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]].

On December 23, 2025, Brown signed a two-year, $6.6 million contract extension with the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web|title=OL Ben Brown signs two-year extension with the Patriots|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/ol-ben-brown-signs-two-year-extension-with-the-patriots|access-date=December 26, 2025|website=nbcsports.com|language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Brown is the seventh member of his family to play for the Rebels.<ref name=":0" /> Brown's grandfather [[Allen Brown]] also played professional football with the [[Green Bay Packers]], winning [[Super Bowl I]] and [[Super Bowl II]].<ref>{{Cite AV media|title=Ben Brown following in his grandfather's footsteps 👏 #patriots #superbowl #nfl #shorts|url=https://www.youtube.com/shorts/vgJnOPebVfU|language=en|access-date=2026-01-31|via=www.youtube.com}}</ref>

'''Barryn Sorrell''' (born December 22, 2002)<ref name=birthday /> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Green Bay Packers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] and was selected by the Packers in the fourth round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Sorrell grew up in [[New Orleans, Louisiana]] and attended [[Holy Cross School (New Orleans)|Holy Cross School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Danny |date=December 28, 2023 |title=Happy he's back in New Orleans, Texas edge rusher Barryn Sorrell preps for the Sugar Bowl |url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/college/longhorns/football/2023/12/28/barryn-sorrell-texas-football-sugar-bowl-cfp-new-orleans-hometown-nfl-draft-playoff-longhorns-edge/72040279007/ |access-date=January 31, 2025 |website=Austin American-Statesman |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewis |first=Ted |date=December 28, 2023 |title=This Texas linebacker and New Orleans native is home, happy to dish out restaurant advice |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/colleges/texas-barryn-sorrell-new-orleans-native-happy-at-home/article_6ecc92ce-a5e1-11ee-9774-a3370928a506.html |access-date=January 31, 2025 |website=NOLA.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="TheBeast">{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |title=The Beast: 2025 NFL Draft Guide |url=https://static01.nyt.com/athletic/uploads/wp/2025/04/09073220/2025-Beast-v02.pdf |url-access=subscription |access-date=April 9, 2025 |website=[[The Athletic]] |pages=292}}</ref> He was ranked as the 54th strong-side defensive-end in the country and the 840th ranked player overall according to [[247Sports]]. He was rated a three-star recruit and originally committed to play college football at [[Northwestern Wildcats football|Northwestern]] before flipping to [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dabe |first=Chris |date=December 14, 2020 |title=Prep notes: 2 more decommit from Arizona; Holy Cross defensive end Barryn Sorrell to decide Wednesday |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/high_schools/prep-notes-2-more-decommit-from-arizona-holy-cross-defensive-end-barryn-sorrell-to-decide/article_bf34551a-3e26-11eb-8712-0b928db34c05.html |access-date=January 31, 2025 |website=NOLA.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/player/barryn-sorrell-46099427/high-school-248046|title=Barryn Sorrell, Holy Cross, Defensive Line|website=247sports.com|date=July 13, 2021|access-date=October 6, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.burntorangenation.com/2020/12/16/22177360/barryn-sorrell-commits-signs-texas-longhorns-early-signing-day-2021|title=3-star DL Barryn Sorrell commits to Texas|website=Burnt Orange Nation|first=Daniel|last=Seahorn|date=December 16, 2020|access-date=October 6, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
During Sorrell's true freshman season in 2021, he played in six games and finished the season with three solo tackles, four assisted tackles, and one tackle for loss for three yards.<ref>{{cite web |last=Moyle |first=Nicholas |date=September 6, 2022 |title=Why Texas DE Barryn Sorrell could be key to upsetting Alabama |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/longhorns/article/Why-DE-Barryn-Sorrell-could-be-key-to-Texas-17422901.php |access-date=April 19, 2026 |website=San Antonio Express-News}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/barryn-sorrell-1/gamelog/2021/|title=Barryn Sorrell 2021 Gamelog|website=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=October 6, 2023}}</ref> During the 2022 season, he played in 13 games and started 10 of them, finishing the season with 44 total tackles (16 solo and 28 assisted), nine tackles for loss for 55 yards, 5.5 sacks for 46 yards, seven quarterback hurries, one pass breakup and one forced fumble.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/barryn-sorrell-1/gamelog/2022/|title=Barryn Sorrell 2022 Gamelog|website=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=October 6, 2023}}</ref> During the 2023 season, he played in and started all 14 games, finishing the season with 37 total tackles (17 solo and 20 assisted), 4.5 tackles for loss for 33 yards and four sacks for 32 yards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/barryn-sorrell-1/gamelog/2023/|title=Barryn Sorrell 2023 Gamelog|website=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=April 5, 2024}}</ref>

Sorrell announced that he would return for the 2024 season.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/texas/football/texas-longhorns-barryn-sorrell-returns-senior-season-college-football-playoff-2024|title=Longhorns EDGE Barryn Sorrell Coming Back Announces Return to Texas|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|first=Cole|last=Thompson|date=January 7, 2024|access-date=April 5, 2024}}</ref> He finished the year with 44 tackles and six sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yum |first=Caleb |date=January 23, 2025 |title=NFL draft: Scouting report for Texas football edge Barryn Sorrell |url=https://www.statesman.com/story/sports/college/longhorns/football/2025/01/23/barryn-sorrell-nfl-draft-2025-rankings-texas-football/77850195007/ |access-date=January 31, 2025 |website=Austin American-Statesman |language=en-US}}</ref>

Sorrell made his NFL debut in Week 2 against the [[Washington Commanders]], recording one tackle and 0.5 sacks in the 27–18 win. [[South Florida Bulls|South Florida]] (2021–2022) | undraftedyear = 2024 | pastteams = * [[Miami Dolphins]] ({{NFL Year|2024}})* * [[Indianapolis Colts]] ({{NFL Year|2025}}–present)* | status = Active | highlights = | statseason = | statweek = | statlabel1 = | statvalue1 = | statlabel2 = | statvalue2 = | pfr = MatoBa00 }} '''Bayron Matos''' (born December 8, 2000){{Cite web|url=https://gousfbulls.com/sports/football/roster/bayron-matos/13536|publisher=[[South Florida Bulls]]|title=Bayron Matos}}{{Cite news|url=https://eldia.com.do/bayron-matos-el-dominicano-que-suena-con-llegar-a-la-nfl/|newspaper=[[El Día (La Plata)|El Día]]|title=Bayron Matos, el dominicano que sueña con llegar a la NFL|date=March 17, 2024|language=Spanish}} is a Dominican professional [[American football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). After growing up in the Dominican Republic, he moved to the U.S. in high school and played basketball. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico Lobos]] and [[South Florida Bulls men's basketball|South Florida Bulls]] from 2019–20 to 2021–22, before switching to football in 2022. He is a participant in the NFL's [[International Player Pathway Program]] (IPPP). ==Early life== Matos was born in [[Los Mina]], Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.{{Cite news|url=https://us.as.com/nfl/bayron-matos-un-dominicano-que-suena-con-jugar-en-la-nfl-n/|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=Spanish|title=Bayron Matos, un dominicano que sueña con jugar en la NFL|date=January 18, 2024|author=Guillermo Vazquez, Luis}} He grew up playing [[baseball]], the country's most popular sport, and was considered a talented [[pitcher]] and [[outfielder]], being able to throw at speeds in the low 90s.{{Cite web|url=https://www.americanfootballinternational.com/2024-nfl-international-player-pathway-spotlight-bayron-matos-ol-dominican-republic/|website=American Football International|author=Malchow, Alex|title=2024 NFL International Player Pathway spotlight: Bayron Matos, OL, Dominican Republic|date=January 22, 2024}} He liked [[basketball]], however, and so he gave up baseball and moved to the United States at age 16 to pursue a professional basketball career.{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/mississippi-state/Article/Mississippi-State-basketball-commit-Bayron-Matos-turns-down-baseball-opportunities-for-basketball-133556549/|website=[[247Sports]]|title=Bayron Matos: From MLB Prospect to Bulldog Basketball Commit|date=July 10, 2019|author=Jones, Paul|url-access=subscription}} Matos played against [[Wander Franco]] and he credits the brother of [[Manuel Margot]] for teaching him the game of baseball.{{cite web |last1=Layberger |first1=Tom |title=Bayron Matos’ Journey Stretches From Dominican Baseball Fields To The Gridiron At USF |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tomlayberger/2022/09/02/bayron-matos-journey-stretches-from-dominican-baseball-fields-to-the-gridiron-at-usf/ |website=Forbes |access-date=24 November 2025 |language=en}} Matos moved to [[Chattanooga, Tennessee]], and began attending [[Hamilton Heights Christian Academy]], but initially spoke no English, learning some phrases through [[Google Translate]].{{Cite web|url=https://gousfbulls.com/news/2021/11/12/mens-basketball-bored-on-the-diamond-matos-found-his-calling-on-the-hardwood.aspx|publisher=[[South Florida Bulls]]|title=Bored on the baseball diamond, Matos found his calling on the hardwood|date=November 12, 2021|author=Johnston, Joey}} He noted that for a time, the only English he knew was "I'm hungry": he said, "If somebody asked how I was doing, I said, 'I'm hungry.'" He was a top player at the school, being the state leader in [[double-double]]s and [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] while helping them win a state championship. He had 16 [[athletic scholarship]] offers coming out of high school and was ranked a three-star recruit, the third-best player in the state and the 16th-best nationally.{{by who|date=February 2026}} He initially committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State Bulldogs]] but later flipped to the [[New Mexico Lobos men's basketball|New Mexico Lobos]]. ==College career== Matos [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] at New Mexico in the 2019–20 season and debuted in the 2020–21 season, in which he played 20 games and started 15, totaling an average of 6.0 points and 4.1 rebounds per game. He entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]] after the season.{{Cite news|url=https://www.abqjournal.com/news/local/lobo-notes-looking-to-move-on-matos-no-longer-a-part-of-workouts/article_4f275d09-c6d2-5708-95a7-7b3e63a5e5d3.html|newspaper=[[Albuquerque Journal]]|title=Lobo notes: Looking to move on, Matos no longer a part of workouts|author=Grammer, Geoff|date=April 14, 2021}} He ultimately transferred to the [[South Florida Bulls men's basketball|South Florida Bulls]].{{Cite web|url=https://usf.rivals.com/news/south-florida-bulls-land-forward-transfer-bayron-matos|website=[[Rivals.com]]|title=South Florida Bulls land forward transfer Bayron Matos|date=April 27, 2021|author=Wood, Russ}} Matos appeared in 28 games, four as a starter, for the Bulls in the 2021–22 season, averaging 10.6 minutes per game while posting 1.5 points and 2.7 rebounds per game. Matos joined the [[South Florida Bulls football]] team as a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] in 2022.{{Cite web|url=https://www.fox13news.com/news/usfs-matos-trades-basketball-court-for-gridiron-glory|publisher=[[WTVT]]|title=USF's Matos trades basketball court for gridiron glory|author=Barie, Sean|date=August 24, 2022}} Initially a [[defensive lineman]] and [[special teams]] player, he was later moved to [[offensive tackle]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/mundo/noticias/nacidos-para-jugar-bayron-matos-el-atleta-dominicano-que-da-pasos-solidos-rumbo-a-la-nfl|publisher=[[National Football League]]|title=Nacidos para jugar: Bayron Matos, el atleta dominicano que da pasos sólidos rumbo a la NFL |author=López Yes, Ricardo|date=March 21, 2024}} He briefly played on special teams and defensive end during the 2022 season.{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5450359/2024/04/27/bayron-matos-travis-clayton-nfl-draft-international-pathway-mailata/ | title=Could one of these international NFL Draft prospects be the next Jordan Mailata? }} ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 7 1/8 | weight = 313 | dash = 4.88 | ten split = 1.77 | twenty split = 2.89 | shuttle = 4.77 | cone drill = 7.64 | vertical = 28.0 | broad ft = 9 | broad in = 5 | bench = 17 | arm span = 35 1/4 | hand span = 10 7/8 | note = All values from NFL [[International Player Pathway Program|IPPP]] [[Pro Day]]{{Cite web |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=1059945&DraftYear=2024 |title=Bayron Matos College Football Profile |website=DraftScout.com |access-date=August 17, 2024}} }} ===Miami Dolphins=== In January 2024, Matos was announced as one of 16 players selected for the [[National Football League]]'s [[International Player Pathway Program]] (IPPP), designed to give opportunities in the league to foreign players.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-announces-international-pathway-program-class-of-2024|publisher=[[National Football League]]|title=NFL announces International Pathway Program Class of 2024 |date=January 18, 2024}} He trained at [[IMG Academy]] and has been praised by NFL analyst [[Scott Pioli]] for his skills and size.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/three-players-to-watch-at-international-player-pathway-program-workout|publisher=[[National Football League]]|title=Three prospects to watch at International Player Pathway program workout |author=Pioli, Scott|date=March 18, 2024}} Despite being {{convert|6|ft|7|in}} and {{convert|313|lb|kg}}, he ran a 4.88 [[40-yard dash]] at his [[pro day]], which would have been the best among all linemen at the [[NFL Scouting Combine]]. He was eligible to be selected at the [[2024 NFL draft]] and was considered a potential late-round pick. He ultimately was not selected in the draft, but afterwards was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]] as an [[undrafted free agent]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/bulls/2024/04/27/bayron-matos-dolphins-undrafted-free-agent-usf-jeff-scott-nfl-draft/|newspaper=[[Sun Sentinel]]|title=Dolphins reach agreements with undrafted rookies after draft, including prospect who never played a college snap |date=April 27, 2024|author=Furones, David}} He was waived on August 27, and re-signed to the practice squad.{{cite web|title=Miami Dolphins Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-make-roster-moves-8-27-24|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=August 27, 2024}}{{cite web|title=Miami Dolphins Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-make-roster-moves-8-28-24|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=August 28, 2024}} He signed a reserve/future contract on January 7, 2025. On July 23, 2025 Matos suffered an injury at Miami Dolphins 2025 Training Camp. Team trainers came out in to the field but later Matos had to be airlifted to a hospital in the Miami-Dade area. On August 26, 2025, Matos was waived by the Dolphins with an injury designation as part of final roster cuts.{{cite web |title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-08262025 |website=miamidolphins.com |access-date=27 August 2025}} ===Indianapolis Colts=== On October 14, 2025, Matos signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]]' practice squad.{{cite web |title=Colts sign T Bayron Matos to practice squad, release T Marcellus Johnson from practice squad |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-t-bayron-matos-to-practice-squad-release-t-marcellus-johnson-from-practice-squad |website=Colts.com |access-date=15 October 2025}} He signed a reserve/future contract with Indianapolis on January 5, 2026.{{cite web|title=Colts sign 16 players to reserve/future contracts, sign LB Austin Ajiake to one-year contract extension|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-16-players-to-reserve-future-contracts-sign-lb-austin-ajiake-to-one-year-contract-extension|website=Colts.com|date=January 5, 2026}} ==Personal life== Matos is the son of Jose and Kirsten Matos. He has one sibling, Ismael.{{cite web |title=Bayron Matos - Football |url=https://gousfbulls.com/sports/football/roster/bayron-matos/13536 |website=USF Athletics |access-date=8 June 2024 |language=en}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.colts.com/team/players-roster/bayron-matos/ Indianapolis Colts bio] {{Indianapolis Colts roster navbox}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Matos, Bayron}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American football offensive tackles]] [[Category:Dominican Republic players of American football]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Santo Domingo]] [[Category:New Mexico Lobos men's basketball players]] [[Category:South Florida Bulls men's basketball players]] [[Category:South Florida Bulls football players]] [[Category:Miami Dolphins players]] [[Category:Indianapolis Colts players]] [[Category:Dominican Republic emigrants to the United States]] [[Category:Hispanic and Latino American players of American football]]

'''Benjamin Chukwuma''' (born May 8, 2001) is a Nigerian professional player of [[American football]] who is an [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He previously played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia State Panthers football|Georgia State Panthers]].

== Early life ==
Chukwuma was born in Nigeria and moved to [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] at age 17. After previously focusing on soccer and basketball, he took up football and later walked on at [[Georgia State Panthers football|Georgia State]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Auman |first=Greg |title=Meet Bucs OL Ben Chukwuma, NFL-bound two years after his first football game |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nfl/bucs-ben-chukwuma-nfl-bound-two-years-after-first-football-game |website=Fox Sports |date=April 28, 2025 |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref>

== College career ==
At Georgia State (2020–2024), Chukwuma appeared in 23 games with 12 starts between 2023 and 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last=Awtrey |first=Stan |title=New faces get their opportunities for Georgia State in bowl game |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/state-sports/new-faces-get-their-opportunities-for-georgia-state-in-bowl-game/EQ3SEDPIBRDVPGZYT3TCAYBM2Q/ |work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Haalboom |first=Colin |title=Bucs hand biggest UDFA deal in the NFL to rookie who just picked up football |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/buccaneers/news/tampa-bay-buccaneers-hand-biggest-udfa-deal-nfl-rookie-who-just-picked-up-football-ben-chukwuma |website=Sports Illustrated |access-date=August 8, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ben Chukwuma – 2024 Football Roster |url=https://georgiastatesports.com/sports/football/roster/ben-chukwuma/7056 |website=GeorgiaStateSports.com |access-date=September 17, 2025}}</ref>

'''Beau Stephens''' (born November 1, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes]] and was selected by the Seahawks in the fifth round of the [[2026 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Stephens was born November 1, 2002, and attended [[Blue Springs R-IV School District|Blue Springs High School]] in [[Blue Springs, Missouri]].<ref name="iowa">{{cite web |title=Beau Stephens |website=University of Iowa Athletics |url=https://hawkeyesports.com/sports/football/roster/player/beau-stephens |access-date=December 6, 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251223023626/https://hawkeyesports.com/sports/football/roster/player/beau-stephens |archive-date=December 23, 2025}}</ref> He played on the school's [[High school football|football]] team as an [[offensive lineman]] and [[defensive lineman]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Wallace |first=Ryan |title=Sideline Summary: Blue Springs vs. Lee's Summit North |work=GoPowercat |publisher=[[247Sports]] |url=https://247sports.com/college/kansas-state/longformarticle/football-recruiting-kansas-city-blue-springs-wildcats-lees-summit-north-broncos-missouri-class-6-kc-kcmo-2020-recruiting-2021-recruiting-135675126/#1272616 |date=September 26, 2019 |access-date=December 6, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251223023916/https://247sports.com/college/kansas-state/longformarticle/football-recruiting-kansas-city-blue-springs-wildcats-lees-summit-north-broncos-missouri-class-6-kc-kcmo-2020-recruiting-2021-recruiting-135675126/#1272616 |archive-date=December 23, 2025}}</ref> He was a three-year [[team captain]] and was named first-team all-state on offense in his junior season. He also competed in [[basketball]] and [[wrestling]].<ref name="iowa" /> Stephens was rated a four-star [[college football]] recruit by [[247Sports]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Beau Stephens, Iowa, Offensive Line |website=[[247Sports]] |url=https://247sports.com/player/beau-stephens-46085237/ |access-date=December 28, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240905170006/https://247sports.com/Player/beau-stephens-46085237/ |archive-date=September 5, 2024}}</ref> and [[Rivals.com]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Beau Stephens |website=[[On3.com]] |url=https://www.on3.com/rivals/beau-stephens-9544/ |access-date=December 28, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010142504/https://www.on3.com/rivals/beau-stephens-9544/ |archive-date=October 10, 2025}}</ref> and a three-star recruit by [[ESPN]];<ref>{{cite web |title=Beau Stephens Offensive Tackle Recruiting Profile |website=[[ESPN]] |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/240194/beau-stephens |access-date=December 28, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250822050802/https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/240194/beau-stephens |archive-date=August 22, 2025}}</ref> he committed to play for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Bohnenkamp |first=John |title=Class Of 2021 Breakdown: Beau Stephens |work=Iowa Hawkeyes on SI |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |url=https://www.si.com/college/iowa/football/2021-breakdown-beau-stephens-062720 |date=June 27, 2020 |access-date=December 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251223024109/https://www.si.com/college/iowa/football/2021-breakdown-beau-stephens-062720 |archive-date=December 23, 2025}}</ref>
